https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBM.resumo: A Hitachi Energy assinou seu primeiro contrato HMAX Energy no Brasil com a BCR-i Brasil, um grupo internacional especializado em gestão de infraestrutura, serviços técnicos e soluções de eficiência operacional. O acordo visa aprimorar a disponibilidade, a confiabilidade e a resiliência da infraestrutura energética crítica que atende ao crescente setor de data centers no Brasil. Este acordo ocorre em um momento em que o Brasil se consolida como um mercado estratégico para investimentos em data centers, impulsionado pela crescente demanda por inteligência artificial, computação em nuvem e digitalização. Segundo projeções da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE)*, espera-se que o consumo de eletricidade no Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) cresça 4% ao ano até 2030, sendo a expansão dos data centers um dos principais motores desse crescimento. Até 2030, a carga elétrica total deve atingir 98,8 GW, o que ressalta a importância de uma infraestrutura energética confiável e resiliente para operações digitais de missão crítica. “Garantir a máxima confiabilidade no fornecimento de energia é fundamental para atender a setores que exigem alta disponibilidade, como os data centers. Nossa parceria com a Hitachi Energy, por meio deste contrato de serviços de longo prazo e caráter inovador, nos permite combinar nossa expertise no fornecimento de energia limpa com soluções avançadas de manutenção preditiva. O acordo reforça o compromisso da BCR-i Brasil com a excelência operacional, assegurando desempenho contínuo e eficiência para a infraestrutura de missão crítica de nossos clientes”, afirma Raphael Campos, Head de O&M (Operação e Manutenção) da BCR-i Brasil. Por meio de uma colaboração de longo prazo, o HMAX Energy — um conjunto de soluções de serviços da Hitachi Energy baseadas em inteligência artificial e oferecidas por meio de parcerias de confiança ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida — permitirá que a BCR-i Brasil planeje, preveja e evite problemas antes que ocorram em uma subestação de 560 megavolt-amperes (MVA) operada pela empresa, a qual atende a um data center no estado de São Paulo. Ao combinar monitoramento em tempo quase real, inteligência sobre ativos e profundo conhecimento técnico, essa parceria ajudará a maximizar a continuidade operacional, a disponibilidade e a resiliência de ativos críticos. “Os data centers estão no centro da era da inteligência artificial e operam com a expectativa de 100% de disponibilidade. Isso exige uma transformação na forma como a infraestrutura energética é gerenciada — incorporando mais inteligência, capacidade de antecipação e integração. O HMAX Energy foi desenvolvido justamente para atender a essa necessidade, por meio de uma abordagem de serviço contínua e orientada por dados”, afirma Fernanda Alves, gerente do Service Hub para a América Latina na Hitachi Energy. A parceria evidencia uma transformação na gestão de infraestruturas energéticas críticas na era da inteligência artificial. Com a crescente demanda por eletricidade e a expansão da infraestrutura digital, os operadores buscam, cada vez mais, parcerias que ofereçam suporte durante todo o ciclo de vida de seus ativos. Por meio do HMAX Energy, a Hitachi Energy auxilia seus clientes a planejar, antecipar e prevenir problemas, contribuindo para o desenvolvimento de sistemas energéticos mais resilientes, inteligentes e preparados para o futuro.

artigo.texto: MEMPHIS, Tenn. - From cities to suburbs, data centers are popping up all over the Mid South. FOX13 has learned a new technology campus is planned to break ground in Fayette county. County residents said they moved there for the peace and quiet and a data center is not what they signed up for. “We moved out here to raise a family, said David Garner. "We want to get away from the city.” Garner told FOX13 that surveyors started mapping out the land for a data center a few weeks ago. For weeks, residents said city and county leaders had few answers for them. “It didn't seem like they were being very transparent," Garner said. A city meeting was held on Tuesday night and the leader of acquisitions at Big Watt Digital confirmed the site will create power with natural gas. "That will be determined to be natural gas generation, could be reciprocating engines, could be turbines," the company said. Big Watt Digital claims the company came to the area to leave the community stronger and more independent than they found it. However, residents are concerned about water. "They're going to have to put a well in because there's no city services of water in on this land. So if the water gets contaminated, who will be the ones to let us know who's going to monitor that?" asked Garner. The company's website claims the site will use a closed-loop water recycling system and they're consulting with environmental experts to minimize the impact. Many residents are skeptical stating they simply don't want a data center there. A community meeting about the Fayette county project is Saturday at 10:30 a.m. at lifeline Baptist church in Oakland. artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Sérgio Leverdi – Leilão de baterias: a ANEEL fez a sua parte, mas o contrato de 15 anos nasce sem saber quem paga a conta Publicado 17/11/2026 • 18:14 | Atualizado há 13 horas BREAKING NEWS: Trump chega na China para a cúpula da APEC e é recebido por Xi Jinping Foto: Divulgação/Aneel O armazenamento é a peça que falta para dar potência firme a um sistema cada vez mais solar e eólico. Mas os certames de 2 e 4 de dezembro chegam com a regra de custeio contestada na Justiça, no Congresso e na própria agência. A pressa pode sair mais cara que o atraso. Por Sérgio Leverdi – CEO do LAWINFRA Ao pôr do sol, o Brasil faz todos os dias uma troca silenciosa. A geração solar, que ao meio-dia chega a sobrar a ponto de ser cortada, desaparece em poucas horas, exatamente quando as famílias chegam em casa, acendem as luzes, ligam o chuveiro e o ar-condicionado. O vento, por sua vez, sopra quando quer, e não quando o sistema precisa. O Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) tem energia renovável em abundância, mas nem sempre tem potência firme no horário de ponta. É esse o problema que os dois Leilões de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro pretendem começar a resolver. Serão os primeiros certames do país dedicados exclusivamente a sistemas de armazenamento em baterias, e chegam à reta final cercados de uma pergunta que deveria ter sido respondida antes de qualquer edital: quem paga a conta? A matriz elétrica brasileira mudou de natureza em poucos anos. Eólicas e solares passaram a responder por parcela crescente da oferta, e isso é motivo de orgulho. Mas são fontes que dependem do clima. Entregam muita energia ao longo do dia e do ano, mas não garantem, por si sós, a potência que o operador precisa ter à disposição no momento exato em que a demanda atinge o pico. Em 2025, segundo dados da ANEEL, o corte de geração chegou a 20,6% da capacidade das usinas eólicas e solares integradas ao sistema. Há energia sobrando em certas horas e faltando flexibilidade em outras. A bateria resolve exatamente esse descompasso, armazenando a energia nas horas de sobra e devolvendo na ponta, em resposta a comandos do ONS. O desenho aprovado é exigente e coerente com essa missão: os projetos devem oferecer disponibilidade mínima de 30 MW, sustentar a potência máxima por quatro horas a cada ciclo, operar em até dois ciclos diários, com limite de 366 ciclos anuais, recarregar completamente em até seis horas e ter eficiência total mínima de 85%. Os sistemas também deverão ter capacidade de formação de rede, o chamado grid forming, verificada pelo ONS como condição para a entrada em operação. Os contratos terão 15 anos, com início em agosto de 2028, e remunerarão a disponibilidade de potência por meio de receita fixa anual paga em 12 parcelas, sujeita a reduções conforme o desempenho, independentemente do acionamento. O primeiro certame, em 2 de dezembro, é destinado a projetos que atendam aos requisitos mínimos de conteúdo nacional estabelecidos pelo BNDES, com preço inicial de R$ 1,76 milhão por MW/ano. O segundo, em 4 de dezembro, contempla os demais sistemas, com preço inicial de R$ 1,58 milhão por MW/ano. O interesse do mercado é inequívoco. No cadastramento junto à EPE, foram inscritos mais de 6 mil projetos, somando 296.807 MW, recorde de participação em certames do setor elétrico. Segundo estimativas do TCU citadas na ação da Abeeólica, de que trato adiante, os contratos dos leilões podem movimentar entre R$ 108 bilhões e R$ 153 bilhões ao longo de sua duração. A bateria não é um luxo tecnológico. É a peça que permite a um sistema cada vez mais renovável continuar confiável na hora em que o sol se põe. É justo reconhecer o esforço da ANEEL. Em 27 de outubro, a Diretoria aprovou por unanimidade os dois editais, sob a relatoria do diretor Gentil Nogueira, e o voto melhorou o desenho em pontos relevantes. A faixa de referência das garantias financeiras vinculadas às exigências patrimoniais caiu de R$ 9,8 milhões para R$ 6 milhões por MW. A garantia de proposta foi fixada em R$ 60 mil por MW de disponibilidade máxima ofertável, e a garantia de fiel cumprimento e o patrimônio líquido mínimo em R$ 600 mil por MW vinculado ao lance, cada um. Usinas com contratos regulados poderão participar em associação com baterias. O relator rejeitou excludentes de responsabilidade por atraso na conexão, mas, em contrapartida, previu que a temporada de acesso de 2027 terá mecanismo específico para os vencedores, encurtando o processo em pelo menos dois meses. É regulação que reduz risco sem transferi-lo ao consumidor. Mais importante: o relator percebeu o tamanho do problema do custeio e fez o que estava ao seu alcance. Adotou, no edital, um termo genérico para o pagador do encargo, justamente para que o certame pudesse absorver uma eventual mudança legislativa. Classificou o custeio como o tema mais controverso dos certames e registrou que a discussão no Congresso não afasta a obrigação da agência de cumprir a regra vigente. O diretor-geral, Sandoval Feitosa, foi preciso: o edital pode ficar abstrato, mas o contrato “não tem que especificar quem deve pagar”. “A única certeza que a gente tem é que a ANEEL vai cumprir a lei”, completou Feitosa. Aí está o ponto. A ANEEL não tinha como desatar esse nó, porque o nó está na lei. A Lei nº 15.269/2025 alterou a Lei nº 10.848/2004 e estabeleceu que, no caso de sistemas de armazenamento por baterias, os custos da contratação de reserva de capacidade serão rateados exclusivamente entre os geradores de energia, conforme regulamentação da ANEEL. Agência reguladora não revoga lei, apenas executa. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC A regra criou uma exceção ao modelo geral de custeio da reserva de capacidade. Nas demais modalidades, os encargos são distribuídos entre os usuários finais de energia elétrica. Nas baterias, recaem apenas sobre a geração. E

artigo.texto: SPARTANBURG — Spartanburg County Council on Nov. 16 gave final approval for development agreements for three data centers, including the NorthMark and Valara data center on Pine Street, the data center on Jones Road and the AIB data center at the Tyger River Industrial Park. Council also gave first reading for special source revenue credit agreements and development agreements for three new data centers from AIB — two 50-megawatt data centers and one 65-megawatt data center — that are located in the Tyger River Industrial Park and powered by solid oxide fuel systems. Three new data centers Approval of three new data centers comes after county council members amended their data center moratorium last month to allow data centers under 65 megawatts to be built less than a mile from each other and generate their own power. The three new AIB data center proposals, plus the one approved on final reading, represent a capital investment of more than $8 billion in Spartanburg County. Together, the four AIB data centers will provide around 215 megawatts of computing power. Adding in $2.8 billion NorthMark and $1.5 billion Jones Road data centers takes the total projected data center capital investment to more than $12.3 billion and the total data processing power to 737 megawatts. The three new AIB data centers, in addition to any property taxes they’ll owe, will pay a combined $39 million to be doled out to county charitable and nonprofit causes over the next 15 years. Under the arrangement, the county will direct where the funds go, but the company may veto an allocation if the cause doesn’t align with company values. The first AIB data center that was approved on final reading will pay $12.6 million into the community benefit fund. The Jones Road data center that was approved will pay $9 million. AIB spokesperson Pierre DuBois said the company was working hard to develop relationships with nearby residents on Griffin Road and had hired an environmental monitoring company to take sound readings. Under the county rules, data centers are now treated as if they’re being built in restrictive developments, which limits noise to 75 decibels at the property line — about as loud as a vacuum cleaner — and 70 decibels between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. Nor can they increase noise by more than 10 decibels beyond. DuBois said company engineers had predicted the noise level at the property line of the first approved data center would be about 63 decibels, which is about as loud as a business office or normal conversation. He also said the data centers would use a closed-loop cooling system using a trucked-in fluid solution and only about 65,000 gallons of water per year for regular office use. “We are also drafting a good neighbor agreement with these neighbors that live on Griffin Road right now, so that everything we’ve told them, everything we have committed to and everything we are currently doing ends up in writing,” DuBois said. NorthMark and Valara With Chair Manning Lynch not present, county council voted to approve the development agreement for Valara 3-2. Voting in favor were Paul Abbott, Jessica Coker and Jack Mabry. Coker and Mabry both lost their primary elections over the summer against candidates who criticized them, in part, for supporting the Valara project from the beginning. Voting against the deal were Grant DeShields and Monier Abusaft, who have both previously opposed the deal on the grounds that it didn’t include enough environmental protections. “We're pleased with county council's decision and appreciate the support of those who recognize the long-term value of this investment,” NorthMark and Valara spokesperson Sarah Knox said in an emailed statement. Even with the tax incentives, the company has projected that it would pay millions in property taxes: $10.5 million in 2026, $12.9 million in 2027, $13.9 million in 2028 and $15 million per year from 2029 through 2045. In addition, Knox said during comments to council on Nov. 16, the company has made $1.5 million in charitable donations. “From the beginning, our commitment to Spartanburg has extended well beyond the boundaries of our property,” Knox added in her statement. “We've made significant investments in environmental remediation, infrastructure improvements, and community partnerships because we believe in the future of this region.” Abusaft has previously said the company reneged on certain environmental promises it made early in the negotiating process and made a counter-offer that came with the threat of a lawsuit. The Southern Environmental Law Center criticized the Valara agreement for failing to include meaningful environmental protections and said it instead protected Valara’s interests over those of residents. “This agreement is a bad deal for Spartanburg and its citizens,” SELC attorney Carl Brzorad wrote in a letter to county officials. “Its purpose is not to protect the community, but to protect Valara.” Spartanburg County Council approved tax incentives for the $2.8 billion, 457-megawatt self-powered data center last year, with most council members not knowing the full scope of the project. This summer, as the data center was being built, county council passed a data center moratorium that limited the scope of projects to no more than 65 megawatts, provided that the data center complied with a host of other regulations governing landscaping, light and sound, and entered into a development agreement with the county. After passing the moratorium, county officials have tried to apply it to the 457-megawatt NorthMark by making the issuance of a second development permit the company needs contingent on the company entering into a development agreement. In the final agreement passed on Nov. 16, county officials still weren’t happy with the company’s plan for noise mitigation, and included a provision that they wouldn’t issue a certificate of occupancy for one of the complex’s data halls until they were satisfied. artigo.texto: POWERGRID Invites Bids for 100 MW/400 MWh Battery Storage Project 20 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Power Grid Corporation of India (POWERGRID) has invited online bids to develop a 100 MW/400 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at the NP Kunta Renewable Energy Project in Andhra Pradesh. Identified as Package AP BESS 06, the procurement is intended to support renewable energy integration and expand the state’s energy storage infrastructure. The tender has been published through POWERGRID’s PRANIT e-tendering portal under RFX Number 5002005830 and reference number CC/T/W-BESS/DOM/A01/26/15301. The selected developer will undertake the complete design, supply, erection, testing, commissioning, operation and maintenance of the facility. The installation will be developed as Lot 6 within a wider energy storage programme for Andhra Pradesh. The project is part of a planned 1,250 MW/5,000 MWh battery storage capacity across the state. Designed around a four-hour storage configuration, the system will help manage fluctuations in renewable generation, improve power supply flexibility and support the integration of solar and wind power into the electricity grid. Implementation will take place under the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) framework using a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model. The successful bidder will develop, own, operate and maintain the facility in line with the tender conditions, creating an opportunity for private developers and institutional participants to enter India’s expanding energy storage market. The tender fee is Rs. 25,000, while the tender value and Earnest Money Deposit have been listed as zero in the available notification details. Document sales and online bid submissions began on 14 November 2026. Documents can be purchased until 21 November at 11:55 PM, and soft-copy bids must be submitted by 23 November at 11:00 AM. Bids will open at 11:30 AM the same day. Kapil Mandil, deputy general manager, is the tender-inviting officer. artigo.texto: At RE+ 2026, Sineng Electric highlighted its latest technological advancements in grid-forming technology, power conversion, and power quality management. Showcasing a comprehensive portfolio spanning AI data center energy storage, utility-scale energy storage, solar PV, and power quality solutions, the company demonstrated its capabilities in enhancing grid stability, improving power system flexibility, and addressing the evolving requirements of modern power infrastructure. AI Power Block: Advancing Reliable Power Supply for AI Data Centers As AI data centers continue to expand, rapid GPU load fluctuations, increasing power demand, and stringent power quality requirements are presenting new challenges for grid stability and power supply reliability. At RE+ 2026, Sineng Electric introduced three integrated power supply configurations through a system-level model: Renewable Energy Power Supply, Gas Turbine + Energy Storage, and Gas Turbine + AI Power Block, highlighting flexible architectures for diverse AI data center applications. A key highlight was Sineng Electric’s AI Power Block, an energy storage solution incorporating Sineng’s string PCS on both the grid and load sides, a BESS, and an MV bypass switch. Featuring dual-sided grid-forming control, the solution supports coordinated operation with the utility grid and on-site generation, including gas turbines and gas engines. Serving as a fast-response power and energy buffer between generation sources and dynamic computing loads, the AI Power Block smooths rapid GPU load fluctuations while mitigating the impact of disturbances originating from either side. Its grid-side PCS provides dynamic voltage and frequency support, while the load-side PCS maintains independently regulated AC voltage for critical computing loads, enhancing both grid stability and power supply resilience. Utility-Scale Energy Storage Solutions: Supporting the Evolution of Modern Power Systems Sineng Electric presented its comprehensive grid-forming energy storage portfolio, featuring both string and central PCS solutions compatible with battery energy storage systems exceeding 6 MWh in capacity. The 430 kW string PCS, integrated into 6.25/6.88 MW MV Turnkey Stations, features advanced liquid-cooling technology that reduces temperature rise by 5 K and auxiliary power consumption by 30%. Cluster-level energy management improves battery capacity utilization by 7%, while automated SOC calibration reduces battery replenishment costs. Sineng Electric’s 5/6.9 MW MV Turnkey Stations, configured with 1.25/1.725 MW central PCS units, support 1-, 2-, 4-, 6-, and 8-hour energy storage durations. The design reduces the number of parallel battery clusters by 50%, increasing usable capacity by 0.75%. Its 20-foot containerized design simplifies transportation and deployment. Both string and central PCS incorporate advanced grid-forming capabilities, including 1.5× rated current for 10 seconds, station-level black start, and seamless switching between grid-following and grid-forming modes. These capabilities provide dynamic voltage and frequency support, enhance operational stability under weak-grid conditions, and facilitate greater renewable energy integration. PV Solutions: Delivering High Efficiency and Enhanced Grid Support In the solar PV sector, Sineng Electric displayed its 4.8 MW MV Turnkey Station and 510 kW high-power string inverter, featuring high-efficiency power conversion, intelligent protection, and optimized grid-support capabilities. The 4.8 MW MV Turnkey Station integrates two 2.4 MW central inverter units and a transformer. Equipped with a fault recorder and intelligent I–V curve diagnostics, the solution enables accurate fault identification and localization. Its modular design allows core module replacement within 25 minutes, minimizing maintenance downtime and enhancing system availability. With a voltage disturbance response time of less than 5 ms and stable operation under weak-grid conditions, the solution delivers enhanced grid support and operational reliability. The 510 kW string inverter supports 1,650 V DC input and 1,000 V AC output, enabling optimized system design and reduced LCOE. Equipped with AFCI 2.0, intelligent DC arc fault protection, MPPT-level insulation monitoring, and AC/DC terminal temperature monitoring, the inverter enhances operational safety. Intelligent airflow monitoring, reverse-fan cleaning, and an anti-icing fan design further support reliable operation under demanding environmental conditions. Power Quality Control System Solutions: Enabling Reliable Operation of Critical Infrastructure Sineng Electric showcased its Active Power Filter (APF), designed to meet the stringent power quality requirements of AI data centers and other mission-critical facilities. Featuring millisecond-level dynamic response, the APF provides simultaneous harmonic mitigation, reactive power compensation, and three-phase load balancing. With THDi of 5% or less, the solution supports compliance with applicable IEEE 519 harmonic limits, improves power factor, and enhances transformer capacity utilization. By minimizing harmonic-related losses and associated heat generation, the APF enhances electrical system efficiency and supports reliable operation of critical power infrastructure. Sineng Electric’s participation in RE+ 2026 reaffirmed its commitment to advancing power electronics technology and addressing the evolving demands of the North American energy market. Through continued technological innovation and industry collaboration, the company will deliver reliable, high-performance solutions that enhance grid resilience, strengthen power supply reliability, and support the modernization of energy infrastructure. Cell production at the approximately $3 billion facility began in October. The plant has a planned annual capacity of 20 GWh, with assembly lines capable of producing 40 cells per minute. The cells are being shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky for Fathom midsize electric pickup prototypes. Ford plans to ramp up production in 2027. artigo.texto: A Firmus Technologies pediu ao governo da Tasmânia que seu data center de inteligência artificial em Wesley Vale seja avaliado pelo processo regular de planejamento, e não como um “grande projeto”. O Conselho de Latrobe solicitou que a decisão sobre a instalação de 52 megawatts fosse transferida ao governo estadual, alegando que seu plano urbanístico, de 1993, não permite examinar adequadamente questões como consumo de energia e água e impactos ambientais. Em carta ao ministro do Planejamento, Kerry Vincent, os advogados da empresa classificaram os benefícios econômicos da unidade como modestos. A Firmus estima aproximadamente 70 empregos durante a construção e cerca de 20 postos permanentes. A posição contrasta com declaração anterior de que seus planos mais amplos para o estado poderiam adicionar US$ 46 bilhões à economia local. Principais fatos e números - O projeto prevê um data center de IA de 52 megawatts em Wesley Vale. - O Conselho de Latrobe pediu que a avaliação fosse transferida ao governo estadual. - O Escritório Estadual de Planejamento analisa o pedido de enquadramento como grande projeto. - A Firmus solicita que a instalação siga o processo regular de planejamento. - A empresa prevê cerca de 70 empregos na construção e 20 postos permanentes. - O conselho considera seu plano urbanístico de 1993 inadequado para avaliar todos os impactos relevantes. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores O caso evidencia o risco regulatório enfrentado por operadores de infraestrutura de IA em regiões com regras urbanísticas antigas. O processo escolhido poderá afetar o grau de análise sobre energia, água e impactos ambientais, além do cronograma de decisão, embora os materiais não informem prazos ou custos. Para investidores e fornecedores, a estimativa de apenas 20 empregos permanentes limita o impacto direto da unidade no mercado de trabalho. Também exige cautela a comparação com a projeção de US$ 46 bilhões, pois ela se refere aos planos mais amplos da Firmus na Tasmânia, e não necessariamente ao empreendimento de Wesley Vale.

artigo.texto: Ford starts $3 billion Michigan battery plant using Chinese tech amid US-China tensions Ford starts production at its $3 billion Michigan battery plant using Chinese CATL technology to make cheaper EV batteries for its upcoming electric pickup. Ford Motor has started producing battery cells at its new $3 billion manufacturing plant in Michigan, marking an important step in the company's electric vehicle (EV) plans. The facility uses battery technology licensed from China's battery giant CATL. The plant is located in Marshall, Michigan, around 100 miles west of Detroit. Ford said on Wednesday that production began last month and the first battery cells are now being shipped out. Ford Fathom electric pickup to use new battery cells The battery cells will initially be used to build prototypes of Ford's upcoming Fathom small electric pickup truck. The company's CEO, Jim Farley, has said the truck will compete with Tesla and Chinese electric vehicle makers, according to CNBC. The new plant covers around 2 million square feet and is designed to manufacture lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells. These batteries are expected to help Ford make electric vehicles at lower costs. Ford faces criticism over Chinese CATL battery technology Ford's decision to use technology licensed from CATL has attracted criticism from some US lawmakers and US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Their concerns are linked to the American automaker's business ties with a major Chinese company at a time of rising US-China tensions. Alan Clarke, Ford's vice president of advanced development projects, defended the decision to work with CATL. He said the partnership would help Ford bring affordable battery technology to the US as quickly as possible, according to CNBC. Also read: AI stocks rally: Nvidia, CoreWeave, Nebius, AMD shares jump after $130 billion forecast Clarke said that if Ford wants to make affordable electric vehicles in the US, it must also find the fastest way to develop and manufacture the required batteries. He added that CATL is the world's largest battery manufacturer, making it a suitable technology partner for Ford. The deal will also help Ford learn how to manufacture LFP battery cells on its own. The controversy comes as the US government increases scrutiny of American companies' business ties with China. The development is taking place even as President Donald Trump is meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin this week. In September, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy sent a letter to Ford CEO Jim Farley expressing what he called "profound concern" about the company's connections with Chinese businesses. Duffy warned that Ford's ties with Chinese companies could harm the Detroit-based automaker as well as the wider US automobile industry. However, the White House responded a day later by praising Ford for creating jobs and supporting manufacturing in the United States. Ford Michigan battery plant targets 20 GWh annual capacity Ford's Michigan battery plant is expected to produce around 40 battery cells per minute when operating at its planned production pace. The facility is designed to produce up to 20 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery capacity every year. The batteries will be used in Ford's electric vehicles and its energy storage business, according to CNBC. This is lower than Ford's original plan, which aimed for an annual production capacity of up to 40 GWh. The company reduced its target as it pulled back on some of its electric vehicle plans amid weaker EV investment and changes across the wider industry. Ford expects the new production capacity to help bring down battery costs. The company also said the factory has enough space to increase production in the future if demand rises.The plant uses a high level of automation to manufacture battery cells. Ford plans to ramp up battery production ahead of 2027 EV launch Ford plans to increase battery cell production next year as it prepares for the launch of its Fathom electric pickup truck. The company currently expects the Fathom pickup to launch in the fourth quarter of 2027. The battery cells being produced at the Michigan facility will play a role in preparing the vehicle for production. The new factory is an important step in Ford's effort to build more affordable electric vehicles in the US. However, its use of Chinese CATL technology also puts the company under scrutiny as Washington increases its focus on reducing risks linked to Chinese business partnerships. - ABOUT THE AUTHORDurva More Durva More is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she covers finance, and global news. She brings experience across digital and television journalism, with a strong focus on breaking news, business reporting, and international affairs. Before joining Hindustan Times, Durva worked as an International News Writer at The Economic Times, covering a diverse range of subjects including global politics, business, sports, entertainment, and major world events. She also worked as a Business Reporter with NDTV Profit. A postgraduate diploma holder in Journalism from the Asian College of Journalism, Durva is passionate about field reporting and storytelling. She thrives on the adrenaline of chasing stories, speaking with people from different walks of life, and amplifying voices that deserve to be heard. Her reporting is driven by curiosity, accuracy, and a commitment to making complex subjects accessible to readers. When she is not chasing stories or covering breaking news, Durva enjoys reading books and painting. She loves exploring new ideas, meeting people, and learning about different perspectives. artigo.texto: KIOWA, Colo. - As Colorado communities across the state implement moratoriums over data center development, Elbert County is considering the construction of one on the eastern part of the county off Route 86 near Interstate 70. The roughly 5,700 acre site would be home to the Colorado Plains Ranch Data Center. On Wednesday, project developers and Elbert County staff presented separate presentations to the Elbert County commissioners about re-zoning the land from agricultural to heavy industrial. Bill Rigler, a spokesperson for the developer, said the project would deliver major financial benefits to the county while avoiding the pitfalls of traditional data centers. "There are three reasons why people should hate data centers," Rigler said. "First off, is that older legacy systems use an enormous amount of water that evaporates. Secondly, is that they're oftentimes placed within electrical grid and they tend to raise electrical prices for people, and third is that they're oftentimes placed in residential neighborhoods and residential areas. This project has none of those features." Rigler said the project would nearly triple the amount of tax revenue that comes into the county each year. He said an independent third-party firm estimated the project would generate about $79 million each year in new property tax revenues. "That's enough to pay off the property taxes for every resident in Elbert County, and still have an additional 50 million dollars of brand new annual revenue to play with," Rigler told Denver7's Tyler Melito. Rigler said the project would use a different approach than older facilities. "Not all data centers are created equal," Rigler explained. "What we're trying to do here is to demonstrate that there's a better way to create a data center in a way that can deliver meaningful and significant benefits to the community." He said the facility would rely on closed-loop cooling technology rather than the evaporation cooling used by older systems. But Elbert County resident Stephanie Dieck said she is deeply worried about the proposal. "My biggest concern is is the water," Dieck said to Melito. Dieck said the developers are asking for 188 acre-feet of water per year, which she said translates to 60 million gallons of water. She said that if the proposal is approved, the county would have little power to limit the project's water use. "If it gets approved today, if we cannot get them to tap the brakes," Dieck said. "The county cannot restrict any use of water or water rights so long as the water is used within the county, and the county cannot restrict any building permits based on water rights or water usage." "I was horrified," Dieck said. Rigler addressed those concerns, saying that water would not come from a Denver Water aquifer and not be as much as other data centers rely on. "Older legacy systems like the ones we see in Virginia and Ohio and Texas will use millions of gallons of waters every year, and they use an older technology that relies on evaporative cooling," Rigler shared. "It's called closed loop technology, and it circulates over and over and again and so, for the first phase of this project, the estimated water usage is about 500,000 gallons of imported water." Dieck said the impact would reach beyond the county. "This actually affects the entirety of the state of Colorado because the water table is all connected," Dieck said. She said the site sits near the Big Sandy River, where water can be reached at a shallow depth, raising concerns the project could continue pumping even after nearby wells run dry. Dieck said with the drought Elbert County and Colorado has experienced and the water restrictions they faced, a data center should not receive preferential treatment. "If they're paying the same taxes as we are, then okay, why? Are they allowed to burn all of the water?" Dieck said. Dieck said she isn't opposed to data centers entirely, just not the current proposal, and hoped commissioners will take a moment to realize the harm the facility could cause. During Wednesday's meeting, supporters and opponents of the facility voiced their views on the facility. More than 40 community members spoke during public comment with another few dozen writing in to the commissioners. No decision was made as commissioners recessed the meeting shortly after 6 p.m. and was set to resume at 9 a.m. Thursday. artigo.texto: Governo avalia possibilidade de contestar restrições dos EUA à venda de chips para data centers no Brasil 00:00 / 00:00 1x 0.5x 1x 1.25x 1.5x 2x Publicidade O governo avalia a possibilidade de contestar as novas restrições anunciadas pelos Estados Unidos à venda de chips avançados de inteligência artificial para data centers instalados no Brasil. A medida, divulgada nessa segunda (16), inclui o país em uma lista de cinco nações que passarão a depender de autorização do governo americano para importar componentes utilizados em grandes centros de processamento de dados. Estão nesta situação, ao lado do Brasil: Singapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia. Segundo interlocutores, uma eventual negociação com os Estados Unidos ou contestação das regras não está descartada. Até o momento, porém, o assunto não provocou preocupação significativa dentro do Executivo - e ainda não há uma definição sobre a adoção de medidas em resposta à decisão americana. A avaliação é de que os Estados Unidos têm amplo controle sobre a produção e o fornecimento desses chips, fundamentais para o funcionamento de sistemas avançados de inteligência artificial. O anúncio do governo americano é uma tentativa de impedir que empresas chinesas usem estruturas no exterior para terem acesso a chips de inteligência artificial e treinar os próprios modelos de IA. O tema surge em um momento de pressão sobre o secretário de Comércio dos Estados Unidos, Howard Lutnick, que enfrenta críticas pela condução dos controles de exportação de chips avançados para a China. A decisão vem ainda em meio ao escândalo que provocou a renúncia de Jensen Huang, ex-diretor executivo da fabricante de chips Nvidia envolvido em casos extraconjugais. A saída ocorreu após investigações sobre a relação dele com uma executiva suspeita de espionagem a serviço da China. Nessa segunda (16), o presidente Donald Trump defendeu o retorno de Huang ao posto de chefia. Apesar da fala do republicano, o conselho da empresa não considera o retorno, segundo apuração da agência Reuters. Donald Trump vai para a Ásia nesta semana, onde terá uma reunião com os presidentes da China, Xi Jinping, e da Rússia, Vladimir Putin. É possível que o assunto Nvidia entre na pauta de discussões. O encontro será à margem do Fórum de Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico, em Shenzhen, no sul da China. artigo.texto: Nio's Onvo Brand Launches Alipay Car Subscription as CATL Moves In on Battery Swapping Published on 11/19/2026 at 03:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de Nio's cut-price Onvo marque has found a new route to Chinese drivers: a car subscription. Alipay Zhima Credit and service provider Hangzhou Maodian Changxiangche Technology launched the programme yesterday, covering 1,000 units of the 2025 model-year L90 SUV across six Chinese cities, with monthly pricing starting at RMB 2,999. Nio shares edged up 0.6% to EUR 2.58 on the news. The subscription push lands against a tougher demand picture. Figures from the China Passenger Car Association published today showed retail sales of alternative-energy vehicles at 447,000 units between 1 and 15 November, down 13% on the same period a year earlier. That weakness does not automatically dictate Nio's own trajectory, but it frames how infrastructure and product announcements should be read. A Rival Builds Where Nio Was First CATL said on 13 November it intends to erect 6,000 battery-swap stations for passenger cars by 2027 — a competitor's expansion plan, not Nio's. The distinction matters. A larger swapping footprint industry-wide is not automatically good news for Nio equity: it can signal that more players see value in the technology while simultaneously testing Nio's own position. The technology could gain weight without Nio capturing a proportional share of the benefit. Nio is working its own access routes. Nio Power and Poly Property Group signed a strategic cooperation on 11 November, according to media reports, aimed at building charging and battery-swap infrastructure across the developer's Chinese projects. The agreement names a partner and a concrete field of use, though a signed cooperation is not a finished network — just as CATL's announced stations are not yet built. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Nio? Deliveries Provide the Reality Check A media report on 13 November flagged October deliveries down 15.2% year on year as a drag on sentiment, a session in which the stock fell alongside other Chinese automakers. Against that, the 40,000th ES9 was reported delivered on 11 November — a concrete product milestone that answers a different question than a declining monthly sales figure. Nio's own disclosures add ballast. The company said it held RMB 56.7 billion in liquid reserves at the end of Q2 2026 and reported roughly 335,000 deliveries for January through October 2026. It also pushed back on claims circulating online about its financial and operational condition, calling them fabricated and saying it had secured evidence and filed a police report. Firefly Teases Europe, Q3 Report Dated A second Nio brand has news pending: Firefly yesterday flagged a Europe-related announcement for 20 November. On the numbers front, Nio will publish unaudited third-quarter 2026 results before the US market open on 1 December, covering the quarter ended in September, with a management call the same day. Nio at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. That print is the next confirmed checkpoint — the moment when the infrastructure story gets measured against actual business performance. The question for investors is not whether new partnerships deserve attention, but how much weight they carry given softer deliveries and a rival's planned network. Nio's site cooperation is a concrete building block, not yet proof of competitive advantage; CATL's plans raise the bar that thesis must clear. artigo.texto: European Commission pledges to fast-track review of Ukraine’s emissions trading bill – Environment Ministry Ukraine’s Deputy Economy and Environment Minister Oleksandr Krasnolutskyi said this in a comment to Ukrinform on the sidelines of the UN climate conference COP31 in Antalya. “We very much need to receive a response quickly. They promised to speed things up,” Krasnolutskyi said, commenting on his meetings with European Commission representatives. He explained that, following discussions with the relevant parliamentary committee, the draft law on the emissions trading system had been translated into English and submitted to the European Commission for assessment. “But what is holding us back? We do not have the European Commission’s opinion. It is important for us not simply to pass a law, but to ensure that this draft legislation meets European standards,” the deputy minister noted. Krasnolutskyi added that Ukraine was simultaneously preparing the necessary infrastructure and developing programs to launch its national emissions trading system. The deputy minister also spoke about a memorandum signed at COP31 with the Nordic Environment Finance Corporation (NEFCO). According to him, cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement will enable Ukraine to attract funding for emissions reduction projects by Ukrainian businesses. Speaking about reconstruction, Krasnolutskyi stressed that the choice of technologies would determine how competitive the Ukrainian economy would be after the country joins the EU. “We must rebuild the country using the latest environmentally friendly technologies. This will create a competitive economy. We must not become a country that joins the European Union and constantly asks for assistance,” he said. Among the EU countries with which Ukraine must be prepared to compete economically, the deputy minister named Germany, Sweden and France. As Ukrinform reported, the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) is being held in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026, with representatives from 197 countries taking part. Ukraine has presented its pavilion and an extensive program of events.

artigo.texto: ANTÁLIA, TURQUIA — A terça-feira (17) da COP31 foi dedicada às discussões sobre oceanos, mares, natureza e uso do solo. Seguindo a temática da Conferência, os diálogos realizados no Implementation Hub Pavilion, espaço do setor produtivo brasileiro na COP31, conectaram políticas públicas de transição ecológica a investimentos industriais de alto impacto. O dia trouxe debates sobre estratégias nacionais de descarbonização, modelos de economia circular para a preservação marinha, soluções em minerais críticos e mecanismos de valorização macroeconômica das florestas tropicais. Um dos marcos centrais da programação nesta terça-feira foi a edição especial do Minas Day, voltada à Coalizão de Minerais Essenciais para a Transição Energética. Promovida pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração (IBRAM) e pela Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Minas Gerais (FIEMG), com a presença do governador Mateus Simões, a sessão apresentou dados inéditos do setor produtivo mineiro. A preservação dos ecossistemas aquáticos e a gestão sustentável de matérias-primas integraram o eixo de economia circular ao longo da tarde. O painel promovido pela CNI analisou as tendências regulatórias e os incentivos financeiros para acelerar a transição circular na indústria, contando com a participação da Volkswagen Caminhões e Ônibus, da Associação Brasileira da Indústria de Alimentos (ABIA) e da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (FINEP). Em seguida, a Agência Brasileira de Desenvolvimento Industrial (ABDI) liderou a sessão "Recircular para não chegar ao mar", que reuniu especialistas e lideranças políticas, incluindo o conselheiro da COP31 Carlos Silva Filho, a senadora Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS) e representantes da Associação Brasileira de Energia de Resíduos (ABREN). O debate enfatizou a rastreabilidade da cadeia de materiais e a reciclagem como ferramentas essenciais para barrar o descarte inadequado e o vazamento de resíduos plásticos em rios e oceanos. O encerramento dos trabalhos concentrou-se nos instrumentos de valoração ambiental e integridade de mercado. A CNI e o Instituto Clima e Sociedade (iCS) promoveram um painel dedicado às oportunidades do mercado de carbono para a indústria brasileira, discutindo a precificação de emissões, a regulamentação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões e os avanços do Artigo 6 do Acordo de Paris. Simultaneamente, a World Climate Foundation, em parceria com a Global Optimism, encerrou as atividades com uma reflexão sobre a resiliência das florestas tropicais enquanto ativos macroeconômicos críticos, sublinhando que a conservação dos serviços ecossistêmicos é pilar indispensável para a estabilidade financeira e a segurança alimentar global. O espaço da indústria na COP31 A CNI marca presença na Zona Azul da Cúpula do Clima com o Implementation Hub Pavilion. O espaço é dedicado a painéis e encontros e reúne lideranças empresariais, representantes de governos, instituições financeiras e organizações internacionais para compartilhar experiências, discutir oportunidades e fortalecer parcerias para a transição a uma economia de baixo carbono. O espaço é promovido pela CNI, em correalização com o Conselho Nacional do SESI, o Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Industrial (SENAI) e a World Climate Foundation (WCF). Conta com o apoio do Instituto Amazônia+21, da Facility de Investimentos Sustentáveis (FAIS), do Instituto Clima e Sociedade (iCS) e da U.S. Chamber of Commerce, além do patrocínio da ABDI, da Samarco, da Aegea, da MBRF, da Vale, da Confederação Nacional das Seguradoras (CNseg), do Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração (IBRAM), da Volkswagen Truck and Bus e da Ambev.

artigo.texto: MCDONALD - Concerns about data centers are still among residents after the company Oppadin provided answers to several questions concerning the project. Those concerns were voiced to the village council Wednesday night, as they pleaded with them to consider community feedback. Despite the efforts from Oppadin to answer resident questions, the people in McDonald continued to grow frustrated from the lack of answers provided by council. “We should not have to stand here and beg meeting after meeting for what you on record promised,” said one woman. The questions that were addressed by Oppadin primarily dealt with environmental, economic and utility concerns. People are still hesitant to trust the company, and fear alternative motives from the company. “I think think Oppidan is trustworthy, I really don’t,” one man said. “I’ve seen enough smoking guns throughout my careers and I really don’t think they’re a trustworthy company coming into this village to do business.” Among the several public comments, there were many calls for the Village officials to put the matter on the ballot next May. Another speaker who took a neutral position, says he understands both sides of the issue, but his main concern is the divisive nature of the discussions. “There’s an old saying that united we stand, and divided we fall,” he said. “The last thing, in my elderly years, that I want to see is this village become divided and lose what we’ve had all these years.” Ray Lewis, the Mayor of McDonald, was given the opportunity to address both the Oppidan FAQ and the community comments. He refused to answer any questions. artigo.texto: Ford (F) announced on Wednesday that the first lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells are coming off the line at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, as part of a plan to license China's CATL battery designs. The move comes against the complicated backdrop of using Chinese tech in US made components. The batteries are headed to Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky to power prototypes of the Fathom, Ford's upcoming midsize electric pickup. Ford hopes to build an EV cheap enough to win over gas truck buyers, with the Fathom set to start under $30,000 — and key to that is using lower-cost batteries. "Ford is officially in the battery business. We'll be the first to deliver LFP batteries in the US for mainstream consumer automotive use, and I couldn't be prouder of the Ford team," CEO Jim Farley said on X. LFP batteries don't use nickel or cobalt, which Ford said helps hold down costs, and the chemistry holds up over years of charging. Ford went with prismatic, or rectangular, cells that fit directly into the chassis. That makes the battery pack part of the truck's structure and cuts costs. Ford said the Michigan lines can produce 40 cells per minute, making them among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China. But the technology inside those cells produced some controversy. Ford said its search for a proven LFP design "led us to the world's leading battery manufacturer, CATL," the Chinese giant whose batteries power 30 million vehicles globally. Ford called the deal a "limited technology-licensing and services agreement," not a joint venture. It says it owns the plant, controls operations, and employs the workforce. That hasn't satisfied Washington. In a letter to Farley sent in early September, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expressed "profound concern" over Ford's "reliance on technologies of foreign adversaries." He cited the CATL tech in Marshall, Ford's joint factory with Geely in Spain, and its talks with BYD on hybrid components. Chief communications officer Mark Truby called it a "head-scratcher of a letter" that came "a week after [the] White House touted the very same job-creating Michigan project he's questioning." Ford's official response called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines." With that in the rearview mirror (for now), Ford plans to have its battery pack plant in Marshall running in 2027, ahead of the Fathom's launch. Ford said what it learns there will also feed Ford Energy, its battery energy storage business, which is preparing production in Glendale, Kentucky. Pras Subramanian is Lead Auto Reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram.

artigo.texto: A draft of a bill in the Ohio legislature could allow data centers to qualify as public utilities. That's according to a new report from News 5 Cleveland WEWS, which cites a leaked version of the draft as expanding the definition of “public utility” to include “an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities.” This could open the door for developers to seize land through eminent domain for those facilities. Those working on the bill have denied that that's their intention. 21 News has not been able to independently review the draft legislation language. Rep.-Elect John Boccieri (D-58), currently undergoing orientation has he prepares to return to the state legislature, told 21 News he thinks eminent domain for data centers is a “horrible idea.” “To force a community's hand to take private land, private farmland in many cases, just because a a private owner does not agree to a price — the bill suggests that there'll be a fair market price, but if they don't agree to that price, then they could be taken to court and their land could be seized,” Boccieri said. “That is not what we need to do.” Boccieri said he is concerned the language will get added as an amendment to a “fast-moving” bill in the lame duck session, allowing it to be passed without proper scrutiny and input from the public. Overall, he argued, the state legislature has “shirked its responsibility” to set the standard for data center development statewide. “We certainly don't want this technology going to China, but at the end of the day, we don't want it hurting local communities,” Boccieri said. “You get communities like McDonald and Lordstown and others who are struggling to try to identify what's real, what's not real. We've got to do a better job.” The draft legislation has not actually been formally introduced, state Rep. Dave Thomas (R-65) pointed out. “Any member can draft anything at any time,” Thomas said. “There's no bill. … Nothing's formally tied to anyone.” Thomas said he doesn’t support the idea, and doubts it would pass — especially because in his view, the legislature has worked to make eminent domain more difficult to impose on property owners, not less. “Having more of that kind of resident say-so, property owner say-so, and not forcing something to come to a community that folks don't want is something that we keep hearing consistently,” Thomas said. “So I just don't quite see the support.” 21 News also reached out to state Reps. Tex Fischer, Nick Santucci, Monica Robb Blasdel and Lauren McNally, in addition to state Sens. Al Cutrona and Sandra O’Brien. None of them got back to us for an interview before publication.

artigo.texto: Greenwood County’s Ad Hoc Committee for Data Centers examined proposed setbacks, landscaping buffers and building heights Wednesday as its members continued discussions about how potential data centers could be regulated in the county. Deputy County Manager for Operations Rob Russian and Planning Director Ryan Bland presented information comparing the county’s existing industrial zoning requirements with previously proposed regulations specifically designed for data centers. The presentation reviewed provisions from a previously proposed data center zoning amendment, including larger setbacks, landscaped buffers and screening requirements. “As we looked at data centers previously, hopefully we can use these tools to evaluate how we want to apply (them) to potential new development,” Bland said at the start of the presentation. Under the county’s existing industrial zoning rules, front setbacks are generally 40 feet in I-1 and I-2 districts, with landscaping buffers often ranging from 40 to 60 feet depending on neighboring properties. Bland explained the earlier proposal included a minimum 200-foot setback on a data center property and a 1,000-foot building-to-building separation from sensitive uses that included: residences, schools, day care facilities, hospitals, parks and public open spaces, and places of worship. Proposed landscaped buffers would range from 100 to 200 feet, depending on building size. Along roadways, the proposal called for a 10-foot-high earthen berm with plantings to help reduce visual impacts. Committee member Cathy Miller questioned whether the buffers would be included within the required setbacks or added to them. Russian clarified the buffer would fall within the larger separation distance rather than being added to it. Russian also discussed a visit to a data center campus in Prince William County, Virginia, one of the largest data center hubs in the United States. There’s a 10-building campus has more than 600 megawatts of electrical capacity, with at least six buildings operating. He said an apartment complex was about 180 feet from a nearby data center, a distance that would not satisfy Greenwood County’s previously proposed separation requirements. “180 feet I think is way too close to residential development,” Russian said. Russian said residents and businesses his group spoke with during the visit reported no complaints about the facilities, although he acknowledged those observations were based on a limited number of conversations. During the ad hoc meeting, County Manager Toby Chappell emphasized the proposed requirements are not final and that data centers currently are not permitted under the county’s existing zoning rules. “One, should data centers be allowed in Greenwood County? And if so, question two, under what regulations?” Chappell said, explaining the committee’s responsibilities. Chappell also said the proposed requirements could significantly limit the number of properties suitable for development, with county officials eventually expected to identify potential sites based on infrastructure needs and zoning restrictions. During public comment, resident Adam Jackson questioned how the county would enforce noise regulations if complaints arose after a data center was constructed. “What does code enforcement actually have the ability to do to make sure that that is properly remediated?” Jackson asked. Chappell said code enforcement could issue citations and pursue violations through the courts. The committee also discussed whether to visit an operating data center midway through its remaining discussions or after completing them, but did not decide when to schedule a visit. The committee’s next meeting is tentatively scheduled for 5 p.m. Dec. 14 at Park Plaza, where members are expected to discuss power and heat generation. Future discussions are expected to address wildlife and environmental impacts, air quality, lighting, medical concerns and economic impacts before the committee begins developing potential regulations.

artigo.texto: Boston-based water technology company Gradiant announced November 19 that it is concentrating its core operating business on water infrastructure supporting the growing AI economy, while establishing a separate platform, Entropy, to develop and commercialize its emerging technologies. According to the company, more than 90% of its core operating business now serves AI-related industries, including hyperscale data centers, semiconductor fabrication facilities, and the power and industrial infrastructure supporting them. Gradiant expects its operating business to generate approximately $150 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) in 2027, with an EBITDA margin exceeding 20%. The company reports that its existing order backlog covers most of its projected 2027 earnings and approximately 35% of its 2028 forecast. The restructuring separates Gradiant's established water and wastewater infrastructure operations from three emerging technology businesses. These include alkaLi, which recovers lithium and other critical minerals from brines and wastewater; ForeverGone, which focuses on destroying PFAS contaminants; and Turing, which applies artificial intelligence to water treatment operations. The new Entropy platform, led by CEO Anurag Bajpayee, will provide dedicated teams and development resources for each technology while remaining part of the Gradiant group. "AI runs on chips, and chips run on water," said Prakash Govindan, Gradiant co-founder and CEO, emphasizing the company's decision to concentrate on infrastructure supporting AI expansion. The announcement follows Gradiant's September disclosure of a contract to provide integrated water supply and wastewater treatment infrastructure for a hyperscale AI data center campus in West Texas. That project includes a zero-surface-discharge design intended to support data center development in a water-constrained region. As AI infrastructure development expands into markets facing water availability challenges, treatment, recycling, and wastewater management are becoming increasingly important considerations in data center site selection and operations. Gradiant said the organizational changes will not affect existing customer contacts, project teams, or ongoing contracts.

artigo.texto: Long-duration battery project will support energy resilience in the Winterhaven area IMPERIAL — The Imperial Irrigation District (IID), in partnership with the Fort Yuma Quechan Indian Tribe and CMBLU Energy, has secured $7.2 million in grant funding from the California Energy Commission for the Echo Sands Community Resilience project. The funding will support a 1 MW / 10 MWh long-duration energy storage pilot at IID’s Pilot Knob Hydroelectric Plant near Winterhaven. The project is designed to strengthen energy reliability and resilience for the Quechan Tribe and surrounding communities during extreme heat and other disruptive events. “This funding reflects the value of strong partnerships,” said IID Board Chairwoman Karin Eugenio. “Working with the Quechan Tribe helped make this opportunity possible and will support greater energy resilience for communities in eastern Imperial County.” The Fort Yuma Quechan Indian Tribe is a key partner in the project, helping ensure the pilot reflects the resilience needs of the Tribe and surrounding Winterhaven communities. Tribal participation will include project planning, community engagement and identifying critical facilities that could benefit from greater energy resilience. “Reliable energy is essential to the safety and well-being of our people,” said Fort Yuma Quechan Indian Tribal President Jonathan E. Koteen. “We appreciate this partnership and the opportunity to advance a project that will strengthen resilience for the Quechan people and our neighboring communities.” The pilot will use CMBLU Energy’s SolidFlow technology, marking IID’s first deployment of a non-lithium long-duration battery storage system. The technology uses non-flammable, aqueous materials and is designed to avoid thermal runaway, allowing IID to evaluate an innovative energy storage option with community safety in mind. Results from the pilot will help IID evaluate the technology's performance and determine whether larger-scale applications may be appropriate in the future.

artigo.texto: PrimaMedia, 20 ноября. China is deepening global cooperation in compliance carbon markets and high-integrity credits while leveraging its domestic systems for a green transition. A senior ecology official announced this at an international climate forum in Turkiye this week. The national carbon trading market launched in 2021. The certified emission reduction market followed in 2024. Both use market mechanisms to support low-carbon goals. The domestic market now covers over 8.3 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions. Cumulative trading in carbon allowances has exceeded 1 billion tons. A coalition for compliance carbon markets formed with Brazil and other international partners at a previous global summit. It adopted a new declaration at the current forum. This initiative aims to share experiences, improve mutual understanding of rules, and coordinate different carbon markets. Global climate agreements are driving demand for reliable credits. To address this, China, Turkiye, and Ethiopia launched a joint initiative. It focuses on better governance, closer cooperation, and improved infrastructure for high-integrity credits to prevent environmental risks. Carbon prices guide green innovation and investment. The country is improving project standards to help financial institutions support climate projects. Local pools have already registered over 6,300 projects with total investments exceeding 4 trillion yuan. Through South-South cooperation, the country has trained over 10,000 officials from more than 120 developing nations. Specialized programs on carbon market design will be expanded. This will help these nations build and improve their own systems.

artigo.texto: QUINCY TOWNSHIP, MI (WTVB)- Quincy Township residence gathered at the Quincy Middle School cafetorium this week, to question staff from renewable energy developer EDF regarding a proposed 180-megawatt lithium-iron-phosphate battery storage facility. The 720-megawatt-hour project is slated for roughly 47 acres of prime farmland west of Boone Road and north of U.S. 12, about 6.6 miles east of Coldwater. While EDF Project Manager Kerry Hoffer says the company has not yet decided whether to pursue local township zoning or bypass local rules through the Michigan Public Service Commission under PA Act 233, Tuesday’s session fulfilled the first step required for a state-level application. Many residents in attendance opposed the facility, echoing broader regional pushback from State Rep. Jennifer Wortz, who has consistently opposed similar energy projects in Branch County and across her district. While EDF Project Manager Kerry Hoffer says the company has not yet decided whether to pursue local township zoning or bypass local rules through the Michigan Public Service Commission ( MPSC) under PA Act 233, Tuesday’s session fulfilled the first step required for a state-level application. Wortz says THE MPSC has a history of overriding local decisions when it comes to these types of energy facilities During the informal open house, attendees and local officials raised significant concerns regarding farmland loss, emergency response, and fire hazards—noting that batteries can reignite even after shutdown. Branch County Drain Commissioner Mike Hard highlighted that most residents within two miles of the proposed site are Amish, meaning they lack phones for emergency alerts and rely on horses and buggies to evacuate. Wortz says the reason Branch County is so attractive to energy companies is two fold Township zoning allows battery storage only in industrial zones. The township has only two industrial-zoned parcels, both already in use. EDF rejected an earlier three-parcel layout along U.S. 12 because the land had little tree cover, bordered the Sauk River, and sat near more homes according to documents prepared for the application process In response to community feedback, EDF added plans for sound walls and an emergency entrance off East Chicago Road, while projecting noise at the nearest home 750 feet away would not exceed 55 decibels. EDF aims to bring the facility online by 2031, though Hoffer noted the exact design and permitting path remain undetermined as discussions with local authorities continue.

artigo.texto: 36Kr Exclusive | A sodium-ion battery cathode material manufacturer has secured tens of millions of yuan in strategic investment from Jintou Zhiyuan, and its 10,000-ton production line will be put into mass production in Q4. Source / Enterprise This article contains about 3100 words, with an estimated reading time of 8 minutes Author: Ou Xue Editor: Yuan Silai Hard Krypton learned that Nayuan New Materials Technology (Wuxi) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Nayuan New Materials"), a sodium-ion battery cathode material enterprise, has recently completed tens of millions of yuan in Series A financing, with strategic investment from Jintou Zhiyuan. The funds raised in this round will be mainly used for the construction of the advanced battery terminal integrated intelligent manufacturing base in Ma'anshan Economic Development Zone, and support the development of anode-free batteries and overseas market expansion at the same time. Nayuan New Materials was founded in 2022 by a team of German returnee doctors who have deep roots in the battery industry for many years. Dr. Liu Zhongqing, the founder, once worked at the Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany (Europe's top energy research institution), studied under Martin Winter, academician of the German Academy of Engineering, and has been engaged in the development and research of battery materials and products at the University of Oxford and Schott AG, the global leading advanced materials enterprise based in Germany. Liu Zhongqing believes that the evolution path of sodium-ion battery cathode materials can be summarized into three stages: layered oxides dominated from 2022 to 2023, the industry shifted to NFPP from 2024 to 2025, and NFS will gradually see volume growth starting from 2026. The logic behind this is: Layered oxides share similar processes with ternary lithium batteries, which were easy to industrialize when lithium prices were high in the early stage, but their cost performance disappeared after lithium prices plummeted, and they also have potential safety hazards. NFPP is closer to lithium iron phosphate, with traceable manufacturing processes and application scenarios, so it took the lead in achieving volume growth. NFS has the highest technical difficulty — soft materials produced by low-temperature sintering are prone to absorb water, and are prone to decompose and generate gas under high voltage. At present, Nayuan New Materials has formed two polyanion material systems of NFS (sodium iron sulfate) and NFPP (sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate), with a supporting recycling material system. According to Hard Krypton, the team of Nayuan New Materials has created the original NFS "soft and hard combination + skeleton building" technology, which solves the technical bottlenecks of single NFS material including low compaction density, poor high-temperature cycle performance and easy gas generation through the "AB material system" composed of hard additives and main materials. For NFPP, the "ultra-fusion synthesis technology" is adopted to greatly reduce the powder resistance of materials and improve material performance. NFS (sodium iron sulfate) material (Source / Enterprise) The company has a clear division of labor for the two materials: NFS is targeted at non-ultra-long cycle scenarios such as consumer electronics, light power, UPS and start-stop in the short term, and forms significant cost advantages at the PACK end with its 3.6V high voltage platform. NFPP is targeted at large-scale energy storage and artificial intelligence AIDC scenarios, focusing on long cycle life and high compaction density. NFPP (composite sodium iron phosphate) material (Source / Enterprise) The company judges that NFS does not contain phosphorus, and its BOM cost is less than 10,000 yuan per ton, while NFPP contains phosphorus element with raw material cost ranging from 15,000 to 18,000 yuan per ton. The raw material price difference between the two is about 10,000 yuan per ton. Besides, NFS is the only material that is not affected by the price fluctuation of lithium iron phosphate. Compared with NFPP, it is more suitable for price-sensitive scenarios such as light power, and can replace the existing lead-acid batteries. At present, the NFS material of Nayuan New Materials has achieved mass production on the 1000-ton pilot verification production line in Jiangxi in 2025, adopting the second-generation spray process. The company is further developing the adaptation scheme of hard additives and AB material system to expand the application boundary of materials. In the field of anode-free batteries, the company has made large investments, advancing from small soft packs below 1Ah in the early stage to the development of large cells at 10Ah and 20Ah levels, and plans to produce a complete battery pack of 6020 or 7220 system for on-board verification by the end of this year. At present, the company is cooperating with Schott AG from Germany (solid-state sodium-ion battery development project). Schott provides solid electrolytes while Nayuan provides cathode materials and anode-free solutions, which gradually promotes the transition of battery technology from pure anode-free liquid state to anode-free semi-solid state and full solid state. Interface optimization and nano solid electrolyte coating are carried out on the cathode side, and SEI interface treatment is carried out on the anode side. It is expected that the density of sodium-ion batteries will be increased to 250-320 Wh/kg in the future, and further applied in emerging scenarios such as vehicles, low-altitude aircraft and robots. At the same time, the company is extending its business to terminal integration.
