artigo.texto: A Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) informou seus clientes que pretende interromper o fornecimento de chips para operadores de data centers que alugam mais de 50% de suas unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) para empresas chinesas, de acordo com uma reportagem da CNBC publicada na terça-feira, 17 de novembro de 2026. A política anunciada surge num momento em que as autoridades americanas introduzem medidas adicionais destinadas a limitar o acesso das empresas chinesas à tecnologia avançada de inteligência artificial americana, incluindo recursos computacionais fornecidos por meio de serviços de nuvem no exterior. A CNBC, citando duas pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto, informou que a Nvidia havia alertado seus clientes nos últimos meses sobre as possíveis implicações da proposta da Lei de Segurança de Acesso Remoto (RASA). A legislação ampliaria a autoridade do governo dos EUA para regulamentar o acesso a serviços de computação em nuvem, aproximando as restrições de acesso remoto dos controles já existentes sobre as exportações físicas de semicondutores. Segundo o relatório, a Nvidia também alertou que as regras propostas poderiam gerar riscos legais tanto para os fabricantes de semicondutores quanto para seus clientes. A Nvidia teria definido uma meta de 51% de clientes fora da China O Financial Times noticiou no início de novembro que a Nvidia havia instruído verbalmente seus clientes de data centers a alocar pelo menos 51% de seus serviços a clientes não chineses em contratos futuros. A exigência relatada afetaria operadoras cujos modelos de negócios dependem fortemente do fornecimento de capacidade computacional para empresas chinesas. De acordo com os atuais controles de exportação dos EUA, a Nvidia está impedida de vender certos processadores de IA avançados diretamente para a China. No entanto, os órgãos reguladores têm tido autoridade mais limitada sobre o acesso à mesma tecnologia por meio de infraestrutura em nuvem localizada fora do país. A legislação RASA proposta visa abordar essa distinção, estendendo a supervisão regulatória aos serviços de computação remota. Segundo a CNBC, o projeto de lei foi aprovado pela Câmara dos Representantes dos EUA em janeiro, mas ainda não havia recebido a aprovação do Senado. O Departamento de Comércio dos EUA introduz restrições adicionais ao acesso remoto O Departamento de Comércio dos EUA, por meio do Bureau de Indústria e Segurança (BIS), anunciou na segunda-feira uma regra final provisória destinada a impedir que empresas chinesas acessem remotamente processadores de IA restritos, informou a CNBC. A medida faz parte dos esforços de Washington para fortalecer a aplicação dos controles de exportação de semicondutores e abordar o uso de centros de dados em terceiros países para obter capacidade computacional. A questão atraiu atenção após relatos de que empresas chinesas de inteligência artificial buscavam acesso a hardware da Nvidia por meio de instalações no exterior. Em 5 de novembro, a CNBC noticiou que a desenvolvedora chinesa de IA Moonshot AI havia tentado acessar processadores da Nvidia por meio de data centers na Europa. Anteriormente, em julho, o governo Trump havia acusado a Moonshot de obter acesso aos chips por meio de centros de dados no Leste Asiático. Essas alegações dizem respeito a possíveis métodos de acesso a recursos computacionais restritos e não comprovam, por si só, que ocorreram violações dos controles de exportação. O secretário do Tesouro pede maior fiscalização da Nvidia Os acontecimentos seguem a saída do CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, o que gerou maior atenção às práticas de gestão e controle de exportação da empresa. O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, pediu no domingo uma “reestruturação drástica” na Nvidia, de acordo com a CNBC. Suas declarações vieram na sequência de relatos que alegavam que Huang havia se envolvido em um relacionamento extraconjugal com uma mulher que, segundo as autoridades americanas, era suspeita de realizar atividades de espionagem em nome da China. As alegações relatadas não foram comprovadas como evidências de irregularidades. Bessent também sugeriu que outros executivos da Nvidia deveriam ser investigados quanto ao cumprimento das restrições de exportação dos EUA. Em entrevista à Fox News, ele questionou se a Nvidia teria incentivado vendas que ele classificou como potencialmente ilegais, numa tentativa de aumentar a receita e os lucros. Os comentários representam preocupações levantadas pelo Secretário do Tesouro, e não conclusões definitivas sobre a conduta da Nvidia. Nvidia destaca as limitações da supervisão de produtos pós-venda A Nvidia já abordou anteriormente os desafios associados ao monitoramento de como seus processadores são usados após a venda. Em um documento enviado à Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (SEC) em agosto, a empresa afirmou que buscava cumprir os requisitos de controle de exportação aplicáveis, mas reconheceu as limitações em sua capacidade de supervisionar os produtos depois que eles saem de sua posse. A Nvidia afirmou não ter “controle físico de seus produtos após a venda”, explicando que depende de programas de conformidade operados por clientes e parceiros comerciais. A divulgação ilustra as dificuldades que os fornecedores de semicondutores enfrentam no monitoramento do uso final de processadores avançados, principalmente quando o hardware é implantado em infraestrutura de nuvem que atende clientes em várias jurisdições. As alterações relatadas nas políticas de vendas da Nvidia, juntamente com a legislação proposta e as novas medidas do Departamento de Comércio, podem afetar os operadores de centros de dados que fornecem serviços de computação de IA para empresas chinesas. A Nvidia também é negociada na B3 por meio da BDR (BOV:NVDC34). artigo.texto: Massachusetts pilot program offers free batteries and extra cash A Massachusetts utility has announced plans to use home batteries to help 125 low-income families save money and keep the lights on during power outages — all at no cost to them. If successful, the pilot program could serve as a model for similar initiatives throughout the state, as utilities pursue a mandate to create a more affordable, robust, and equitable electric system. National Grid this month launched BatteryBackup+, a partnership with residential power-storage company Haven Energy that will bring the no-cost batteries to homes in Fall River, a working-class former mill city where the median household income hovers just above half the statewide average. Participants will receive a battery capable of providing at least four hours of backup power, as well as $150 annually for five years. To qualify, residents must already be signed up for National Grid’s low-income discount rate, or meet the equivalent income limits — about $103,000 per year for a four-person household, for example. Haven will handle installation and maintenance of the systems, and manage the batteries’ enrollment and deployment in programs that share their power with the grid to alleviate strain at times of high demand. After 10 years, participants will be able to work with Haven to take over ownership and management of the batteries or remove them. The utility’s overall goal is to develop and refine a strategy for making the grid more efficient and resilient while giving a financial boost to families who are the most vulnerable to soaring energy prices. “We’re really excited about what we get to learn from this,” said Joshua Tom, National Grid’s director of energy transition solutions. The idea of aggregating residential batteries to create benefits for the grid is not new. When batteries work in concert to send power into the system, it can reduce the need for energy from pricier, dirtier plants. In the long term, such arrangements can also help avoid expensive grid upgrades that would be paid for by customers. States are increasingly leaning into the concept. Vermont’s Green Mount Power harnesses this potential with a network of 10,000 residential batteries. Massachusetts’ ConnectedSolutions model, launched as a pilot in 2016, has been adopted or adapted by nearby states including Connecticut and Rhode Island. New Jersey just launched its own program paying residents to share their battery capacity with the grid. Haven’s business model takes advantage of this trend. As in the Fall River pilot, the company handles the installation and management of residential batteries. Haven then earns money from enrolling the equipment in state programs, using some of the revenue to make the investment more affordable for customers. Haven currently operates in seven states — including elsewhere in Massachusetts — with eight more coming soon. In most places, customers pay a monthly fee for their batteries and the company’s services, starting at $29. Fall River is not Haven’s first foray into a no-cost model. Last year, the company launched a program in California providing free batteries to low-income households. So far, the program has contracted with about 2,500 homes and completed installations in about 60% of them. The National Grid pilot is different from the California offering in a few ways. The initiative is an element of National Grid’s Electric Sector Modernization Plan, a strategic document required by Massachusetts in which electric utilities lay out their road maps for modernizing the grid to meet growing demand in an affordable and environmentally responsible way. The utility hopes its experience in Fall River will help it learn more about how to recruit low-income customers and convince them to participate in such programs. “One of the things we’re testing out is how do you get scalable, cost-effective, grassroots customer engagement,” said Steven Caldwell, National Grid’s vice president of energy efficiency and clean transportation. The pilot is also investigating a new question: Can aggregated batteries alleviate strain on a specific portion of the grid, rather than providing only broader system benefits? The utility aims to install 1.2 megawatts of capacity in homes along three grid feeders that National Grid identifies as having reliability and capacity challenges. “They’re targeting areas that maybe haven’t had the infrastructure updates that needed to happen,” said Sherri Bence, Fall River’s municipal energy manager. “We are at this crossroads where we need to start being a little more innovative.” Sarah Shemkus is a reporter at Canary Media who is based in Gloucester, Massachusetts, and covers New England. read next - Virtual power plants New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant

artigo.texto: The largest data centers in the US collectively emit an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of carbon emissions annually â almost as much as Denmark, according to a study published in the journal Nature Sustainability. Harvard researchers found 403 data centers used almost 2% of US electricity, with most of the power being generated from fossil fuels. Sites in Iowa, Ohio, and Virginia accounted for about half the estimated emissions. The study provides the first peer-reviewed estimates of emissions generated by US data centers since the start of the AI boom, although it is not a comprehensive inventory. Without a publicly available list of facilities, researchers pieced together information using a commercial dataset, satellite imagery, and data on the power mix supplying each regional electricity grid. The findings are likely an underestimate as they exclude data centers that researchers could not sufficiently verify, as well as facilities that rely on on-site power generation.

artigo.texto: Pakistan is seeking investment and technological partnerships with Finland in electric vehicles (EVs), battery energy storage and advanced industrial technologies as the country works to expand its electric mobility sector. The opportunities were discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister’s Adviser on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan and a Finnish delegation led by Jarno Syrjälä, Finland’s Under-Secretary of State for International Trade. During the meeting, both sides explored potential cooperation in electric vehicles, battery storage solutions, mineral processing and advanced industrial technologies. Haroon Akhtar Khan highlighted Pakistan’s recent policy initiatives, including the National Industrial Policy, National Tariff Policy and New Energy Vehicle Policy. He said electric vehicles had become an important part of modern transportation and encouraged Finnish companies to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan’s EV and industrial sectors. The adviser also invited Finnish businesses to consider investment in Pakistan’s mineral processing industry. Finnish companies, including Metso and Wärtsilä, are already involved in projects such as Reko Diq. Other Finnish firms, including Nokia and Vaisala, also have an established presence in the country. He added that the government was working to simplify regulatory procedures and remove obstacles to facilitate foreign investment. The discussions also focused on the 14th Finland-Pakistan Business Summit, scheduled to take place in Islamabad on November 16 and Karachi on November 17. The event aims to strengthen business-to-business ties and create new opportunities for companies from both countries. Although no specific Finnish investment, EV manufacturing plant or battery production project was announced, the discussions signal Pakistan’s efforts to attract foreign expertise and technology to support its electric mobility ambitions. Greater cooperation with Finnish companies could help Pakistan develop its EV ecosystem, strengthen battery storage capabilities and expand its industrial technology base.

artigo.texto: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick-and-mortar facilities are located, according to a new study by MIT researchers. The team estimates that additional air pollution from the electricity demands of data centers in 2023 resulted in about 650 premature deaths across the United States. Some Midwestern states had among the highest estimated rates of premature deaths per capita attributable to data centers, even though much of the data center electricity demand was concentrated in Virginia and Texas. The researchers built a modeling framework that captures how the electricity demanded by data centers propagates through the nation’s interconnected power grid. The model also considers how atmospheric conditions impact the formation of air pollution in different regions. The framework identifies power plants across the country whose emissions increase in response to data center electricity demand. In parts of the Midwest, these emissions combine with atmospheric conditions that favor the formation of fine particulate matter, a pollutant that can cause heart attacks, stroke, and lung disease. The researchers say these results underscore the importance of considering unintended regional health impacts of data centers, and how the location and operations of these facilities affect public health on a broader scale. “When people think about the negative impacts of data centers, they usually focus on the neighbors. But our study indicates that the air quality impacts of data centers are very widespread across a large region. Even if you don’t think you are affected because there is not a data center near you, think again,” says Noelle Selin, a professor in the MIT Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS) and the Department of Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences (EAPS); director of the Center for Sustainability Science and Strategy; and senior author of the study. Selin is joined on the paper by Yuang (Albert) Chen, an MIT graduate student; as well as others at MIT, the University of California at Irvine, and Yale University. The research appears today in Environmental Research Letters. Capturing regional impacts The Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory estimated that electricity demands of data centers represented about 4 percent of total U.S. energy demand in 2023 and resulted in about 4.4 percent of the nation’s overall emissions. That proportion has likely increased as new data centers continue to be built at a rapid pace. Many prior studies estimate impacts using average electricity-grid emissions. Like those studies, the researchers assume data centers draw power to run computing tasks 24/7. Their approach also identifies which generators respond to that additional demand hour by hour, allowing them to trace where the resulting emissions and health impacts occur, Chen explains. “Generators that respond to additional electricity demand are often natural gas plants, although the response varies by place and hour,” he says. To drill down on regional health impacts, the MIT researchers developed a modeling approach that enables them to identify which generators are contributing to data center electricity demand within each modeled region. This allows them to incorporate a spatial component into the analysis. They built an electricity system model that simulates how much electricity each generator produces and pumps into the grid every hour. This model also considers how that electricity is transmitted between regions. It gives the researchers data on emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and sulfur dioxide (SO2) for each generator across the United States. NOx contributes to the formation of ground-level ozone, or smog, while both NOx and SO2 contribute to the formation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in the atmosphere. “It was a challenge to gather all the data,” Chen says. “There are more than 10,000 generators in the U.S. grid, and we needed to make sure the data provided for each generator is valid and validated across other data sources.” The researchers incorporated these data into a chemical transport model. This model simulates how pollutants form and travel through the atmosphere across regions. From there, they translated the additional air pollution from data center operations into premature mortality rates using evidence from epidemiological literature. The model estimates that emissions from data centers caused about 650 premature deaths in 2023 (513 from PM2.5 and 137 from smog), which represents about 5.3 percent of the nation’s total electricity-related mortality. “While it is not surprising that any additional source of air pollution will result in mortalities, with data centers, when and where these deaths are occurring are different than you might expect,” Selin says. A pollution mismatch The premature mortality rates were highest in Iowa, Nevada, South Dakota, and Kansas, but the bulk of the electricity demand was concentrated in northern Virginia and in Texas. Premature mortality rates in Virginia and Texas are only about half as much as most Midwestern states. One reason for this mismatch is the interconnected nature of the power grid, Chen says. Generators that respond to the increased electricity demand in Virginia are likely located in the Ohio Valley, where there is a higher proportion of older power plants that generate more emissions from burning coal and natural gas. “Different regions have different mixes of power. If you turn on a major new demand source, by plugging a data center into the grid, you might have to fire up your really dirty power plant to meet that new demand,” Selin says. Plus, due to atmospheric conditions, many pollutants generated in these regions are transported to downwind states. Midwest states like Nebraska and Iowa are traditionally agricultural regions. artigo.texto: Desejando direcionar até 10% do consumo de energia para data centers projetados, Brasil teme restrições de vendas de processadores ONS já recebeu pedido de 159 empreendimentos para acesso aos sistemas de transmissão de 20,7 GW que podem ser afetados pelas restrições dos EUA. Clique aqui e escute a matéria A decisão do governo Donald Trump de incluir o Brasil entre os países que terão restrições para importar chips desenvolvidos nos Estados Unidos para uso em data centers, mesmo que os semicondutores sejam fabricados fora da jurisdição da Casa Branca, pode ter um forte impacto no desejo do Brasil de ser um grande destino desse investimento. Se forem ampliadas as restrições, especialmente para os Data Centers de aprendizado de agentes de Inteligência Artificial, dezenas de projetos que já estão sendo comunicados ao Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) podem ser prejudicados e revistos, embora tecnicamente a exigência apenas acrescente um componente a mais do que eles já precisam para se habilitar no Brasil. O setor de Data Center e Inteligência Artificial foi tema de um dos painéis da Conferência Ibero Brasileira de Energia em Lisboa Portugal (Coniben) horas antes do anúncio americano com executivos do ONS, Sumara Ticom, da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) Thiago Prado, o diretor da Amptank Tiago Barreto de Chaves e o Diretor de Inovação e Novos Negócios da CCEE, trataram do tema a partir das necessidades de energia para fazer funcionar os Data Center. O desafio no Brasil é que o setor pediu ao ONS, entre janeiro de 2025 e outubro de 2026, acesso à transmissão e demais instalações de transmissão, nada menos que 20,7 GW, dos quais 159 empreendimentos com pareceres favoráveis. Parecer de acesso é a autorização para um data center receber a energia que precisa para funcionar. Instalados, eles vão usar quase 20% da demanda máxima de energia entregue pelo Sistema Interligado Nacional. Até agora, o ONS já concedeu 123 pareceres para projetos com viabilidade confirmada que vão exigir 14,2 GW. Desse, 7,9 GW já têm contrato assinado (que vão consumir 3,8 GW) e outros em andamento que vão precisar de mais 4,1 GW. O interesse é tão forte que, dos 159 pedidos, apenas 36 foram negados e 77% (123) aprovados. Prevendo essa demanda, o governo se antecipou e, em 2025, criou o que chamou de Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão (PNAST). Com ela veio um pacote de aprimoramentos regulatórios, criou-se uma fila única de pedidos a sistemas de transmissão de toda essa energia e criou um janela, avaliação conjunta e regras comuns para alocar a margem disponível. Funcionou. Já este ano, quando abriu a primeira temporada de acessos, viu o interesse dos investidores. Ao menos 71 projetos se cadastraram pedindo 2,8 GW. Do total de 65 ( necessitando de 2,6 GW), foram admitidos outros 7, seguiram após verem a margem disponível e 58 desistiram. A informação mostra ao investidor onde a rede pode recebê-lo hoje e ao planejamento onde expandir. O problema é que esses projetos exigem muita energia. O que torna o desafio do governo em fazer com que a chegada dos data centers seja eficiente para o sistema e para todos os consumidores. O que obriga a EPE a trabalhar para fazer os estudos nas regiões com mais pedidos e antever onde a rede já pode recebê-los, tratar dos insumos para que eles entrem sem transferir os riscos. Porém, o fato de, a partir desta segunda-feira (16), fornecedores precisarem de autorização do governo americano para enviar os processadores avançados a empresas brasileiras, com pedidos analisados caso a caso, não deve fazer com que o interesse pelas compras de chips diminua. Mas ninguém gostou de que o Brasil está numa lista que inclui Singapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia, que, segundo a norma, apresentam risco acima do normal de desvio ilegal desses chips para a China ou Macau —alvos de embargos junto com Rússia, Irã, Coreia do Norte, Síria e Cuba. Com base no que já está cadastrado, o que a EPE trabalha e que o Brasil vai multiplicar o uso de energia apenas para Data Center por 10. Sair de um consumo de 3 TW/hora em 2026 para 30 TW/hora em 2036. Muito maior que a própria taxa de crescimento do consumo de energia elétrica no Brasil, estimada em 3,4% ao ano. Isso quer dizer que o Brasil pode ter um consumo muito próximo de 10% de toda a carga do país no horizonte de 10 anos. Essa demanda levou a EPE a criar uma área no site da empresa de planejamento energético do Brasil que tem até acordo de confidencialidade com as empresas interessadas apenas para começar a entender o projeto Data Center. O objetivo é que essas informações possam ajudar a pensar em eficiência energética e no comportamento da carga por sistema mais recentemente. Em outra frente a cooperação a própria Nvidia que passou a além de vender os seus processadores, passou a ajudar a desenhar os parques usando recursos de Inteligência Artificial para fazer o projeto e o desenho e extrair o melhor desses processadores. E como tudo o que está complexo pode ficar mais complicado, a EPE avalia que futuramente, aumentando a densidade de potência dos Data Centers, haverá uma evolução tecnológica com um uso mais intensivo da tecnologia de corrente contínua, o que trará mais complexidade ao planejamento e à operação do Sistema Interligado Nacional. Os Data Centers recebem a energia em corrente contínua e no parque de máquinas, os processadores seriam alimentados em corrente contínua, de modo a dar mais segurança ao sistema. Para a EPE e o ONS, isso representa um novo desafio para o gerenciamento de toda essa energia, o que vai exigir ações para habilitar os sistemas de transmissão.

artigo.texto: CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul ISTANBUL, Türkiye, Nov. 19, 2026/PRNewswire/ -- CATL today announced the official launch of its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye. The facility serves as the country's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, marking a further step in expanding its localized new energy aftermarket service network and supporting the country's shift towards cleaner energy systems. Türkiye sits at the crossroads of Europe, Asia and the Middle East -- a regional economic hub with a fast-growing EV market and a rapidly expanding energy storage sector, where the shift toward clean energy is driving demand for specialized battery support. Its National Energy 2040 plan targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of storage requirement by 2040. Against that backdrop, NING SERVICE is delivering full-lifecycle battery services on both the road and the grid, reinforcing the infrastructure that transition depends on. Located in Istanbul, the NING SERVICE Experience Center represents an important milestone in the collaboration between CATL and Ascendum Türkiye, part of Ascendum Group, offering comprehensive full-lifecycle after-sales support, cultivating local technical talent and accelerating the deployment of advanced electrification and energy storage solutions. Covering more than 1,200 square meters, the Istanbul center brings together service zones for battery testing, diagnosis, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition and retail area presents CATL's system-level capabilities across electric mobility and energy storage, including bedrock chassis, portable power stations, battery protection plates and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center serves as a localized service hub for the region and as a platform connecting partners across the ecosystem. Providing a comprehensive new energy aftermarket service system As CATL's independent aftermarket service brand, NING SERVICE delivers a one-stop, full-lifecycle battery service system that encompass battery diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, training, recycling, aftermarket logistics and warehousing. Backed by CATL's deep R&D and extreme manufacturing capabilities, its services product categories from passenger and commercial vehicles to energy storage systems, setting a new benchmark for new energy service delivery in the region. That capability is delivered through one of the industry's largest after-sales networks: - 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, with the aim of reaching 100 countries and regions by 2027 and 10,000 service locations by 2030; - More than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new energy after-sales service, with a 24-hour response mechanism in overseas markets; - Its deep-repair capability, delivered through a network of 95 centers, covers 76.8% of EV models and 90% of repair jobs; - The Intelligent Eagle Eye System , in use at more than 150 repair facilities, providing full traceability and quality control; - The Intelligent Battery Check System , supporting precise battery health diagnostics, slows battery aging by up to 9.5%; - More than 70 industry standards participated in or revised, and over 200 authorized patents worldwide Strengthening local partnerships and service capabilities CATL is extending its local footprint by strengthening infrastructure and building partnerships in the market. By combining CATL's technological expertise with Ascendum Group's 67 years of industrial heritage and robust local network, the Istanbul center enables CATL to serve clients throughout Türkiye, putting its know-how and rapid-response capability close to where batteries are actually in use. The center anchors a network to all Türkiye and a team of CATL-certified engineers. It also serves as the network's training base, where technicians are trained and certified to CATL's standards before they work on customer batteries, building a local pool of battery service skills that the market will keep drawing on. "The opening of Türkiye's first NING SERVICE Experience Center marks an important milestone in our strategic partnership with CATL and represents the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift," said Tolga Polat, CEO of Ascendum Türkiye. "By combining CATL's advanced battery technologies with Ascendum's long-standing technical service expertise and customer-focused approach, we aim to provide reliable, high-quality aftermarket solutions across Türkiye. We are investing in local technical capabilities, developing specialized teams and strengthening our service infrastructure to meet the evolving needs of the energy and mobility sectors. Looking ahead, our goal is to gradually expand our service network nationwide and build a sustainable ecosystem that creates long-term value for our customers and supports Türkiye's energy transition." "Türkiye has moved into the fast lane on electrification, and demand for aftermarket service will grow with it," said Bruce Li, Co-president of Sales & Marketing and President of Commercial Applications & Aftermarket Business of CATL. "As our first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country, it brings CATL's technology, our training standards and Ascendum's local reach together, so that customers on the road and on the grid are served by people and parts that are already here. From here, we will keep extending our service network across Türkiye, work in step with the country's National Energy 2040 goals, and give the energy transition the service backbone it needs to hold up over time." Looking ahead, NING SERVICE will continue to drive innovation in maintenance technology, service models and network expansion. artigo.texto: Council rejects ordinance lifting Jackson’s data center ban JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Jackson’s temporary ban on data centers will remain in place following a contentious Jackson City Council meeting on Tuesday. After hearing from multiple residents, the council voted down a decision to lift the ban, which Ward 3 Councilman Kenneth Stokes says is needed to “untie the mayor’s hands” so he can bring in economic development. “The only thing we’re doing is asking the mayor to have the opportunity to listen to some of the proposals that are out there,” he said. “We don’t have a clue what they are, but we know these other cities are getting money. They’re building up.” “Why do we as Jackson, the capital city ... Why can’t we have an opportunity to bring money to this city?” he added. Stokes was joined by Ward 1 Councilman Ashby Foote in supporting rescinding the measure. Council members Vernon Hartley, Kevin Parkinson, Tina Clay, Brian Grizzell, and Lashia Brown-Thomas voted in opposition. The moratorium will remain in place until April 4. While it’s in effect, the city will not accept, process, or approve any applications for permits related to new data center projects or expansion projects for existing data centers. Foote believes the atmosphere at Tuesday’s meeting was part of the reason the repeal ordinance failed. “Council meetings have become very negative. We can’t let that negativity keep the city from pursuing economic development that could get the city back on its feet,” he said. Several people attended the meeting to speak out against the proposal, including Ward 3 resident Jackie Warren Tatum, who thanked the council for putting the moratorium in place. “For months, despite Stokes’ absences, we voiced our concerns regarding the negative impact of data centers. And we’re learning about the spills up in Southaven, the unbearable noise, and many other things,” she said. “Please do not repeal and rescind this moratorium.” Tatum was referring to a chemical spill at the SpaceXSI data center in Southaven. Mississippi Today reports that a contractor caused “5,000 to 6,000 gallons of a propylene glycol mixture to spill into a neighboring drainage ditch.” The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) was still determining when it happened, the publication stated. Yolanda Daniel also urged the council to leave the ban in place until the city fully studies data centers and their potential impact on the community. “A moratorium exists precisely to provide the time necessary for fact-finding, public input and evaluation of alternatives. Seeking to terminate that process early raises a simple, but important question: Has the council fully evaluated other economic development opportunities capable of generating jobs, investment, tax revenue, and long-term prosperity for Jackson and Jackson residents?” she asked. “The responsible course remains unchanged. Allow the moratorium to remain.” Want more WLBT news in your inbox? Click here to subscribe to our newsletter. See a spelling or grammar error in our story? artigo.texto: Blendon Twp., MI (WGHN) – Plans for a 100-megawatt battery storage facility in Blendon Township remain uncertain after the Planning Commission reached a three-to-three deadlock Wednesday night. The tie vote means the proposal was not approved. One commissioner who voted against the project indicated he may reconsider if developer Key Capture Energy makes additional changes to its application. Those changes include a more detailed fire emergency response plan, a specific landscaping plan, a designated construction traffic route and limits on changes to the site layout. The proposed 14-acre facility would be built next to an electrical substation near 88th Avenue and Polk Street. Township planners have already placed 22 conditions on the project during a review process that began in August 2025. MLIVE reports that the commission is expected to consider the proposal again December seventh. If the township and developer cannot reach an agreement, Key Capture Energy could seek approval through the Michigan Public Service Commission under state law. The project has drawn strong opposition from residents concerned about fire risks, noise, environmental impacts and its proximity to farmland. The company says the technology is safe. The facility would store electricity during periods of lower demand and release it back into the power grid during peak usage to help stabilize Michigan’s electric supply

artigo.texto: 409% capacity boost: New slurry electrolyte lifts manganese battery storage to 156.2 Ah/L A semi-solid MnO₂ slurry electrolyte has been designed to significantly increase the energy storage capacity of manganese-based redox flow batteries (RFBs) and increase their current density. This system solves problems of poor dissolution and kinetics which manganese-based redox flow batteries face. Redox flow batteries are being investigated as a means of storing energy from renewable sources such as solar and wind. Manganese is a promising candidate for redox flow batteries, however, traditional electrolyte chemistries suffer from poor solubility and kinetic properties. By changing the Mn redox processes within the battery, the amount of active species in the battery can be increased, and the rate of the reaction improved. Slurry electrolyte addresses manganese solubility problems Traditional MnSO₄ electrolytes have limited amounts of dissolved manganese due to common ion effects in sulfuric acid (around 1M). As a result, the system delivers around 38 Ah L⁻¹ in specific capacity. Though increasing the Mn content within the electrolyte using MnO₂ particles in a semi-solid form can increase the active species in the battery, it is limited by slow kinetics of the solid species. Operating current densities have generally remained below 1 mA cm⁻². By adding high concentrations of MnO₂ particles to a traditional manganese electrolyte, a semi-solid slurry was formed. In this system, redox reactions occur between MnO₂ solid and dissolved Mn²⁺. Due to this, the common ion effect is avoided and the concentration of dissolved manganese species is increased to 3.76M. As a result, a much greater amount of manganese active species can be included in the electrolyte. Furthermore, different redox chemistry occurs in the electrolyte as cycling occurs. In particular, during the second charge, reverse disproportionation occurs within MnO₂ produced via electrolysis. Manganese(III) ions (Mn³⁺) are produced in solution. As a result, the overall chemistry moves from slow redox reactions between MnO₂ and Mn²⁺ to fast reactions between Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ in solution. Flow battery maintains high capacity Therefore, a high current density can be achieved in this battery system. The optimized semi-solid electrolyte with 4M MnO₂ demonstrates a specific capacity of 156.2 Ah L⁻¹, increasing capacity by 409% compared to traditional MnSO₄ electrolytes. Even at high currents of 30 mA cm⁻², a high capacity is achieved (over 151 Ah L⁻¹), with an energy efficiency of over 71%. At 1 mA cm⁻², the capacity increases to 183 Ah L⁻¹, meaning that this system outperforms previously reported MnO₂ semi-solid flow batteries. Its estimated material cost stands at roughly US$33 kWh⁻¹. Therefore, this chemistry may be of interest for large-scale energy storage, as material costs affect system economics. Further engineering challenges need to be overcome to implement this system in large-scale grid storage. Capacity loss may occur after prolonged operation due to manganese crossover and agglomeration. To improve long cycling performance, improvements within the electrolyte formulation and membrane may be useful. If these challenges can be overcome, this semi-solid chemistry may allow greater energy to be stored within manganese-based flow batteries, without compromising on operating speeds.

artigo.texto: Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd Announces Execution of MEP Equipment Supply and Installation Contracts for Phase 1B of Indonesia Data Center Source: GlobeNewswire TAICHUNG, Taiwan, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd (the “Company”) today announced that on November 13, 2026, its Indonesian operating subsidiary, PT AGCC AITECH INDONESIA (the “Indonesian Subsidiary”), entered into two definitive contracts with separate contractors for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (“MEP”) works for Phase 1B of the Company’s planned AGCC-JKT01 data center in West Java, Indonesia (the “Data Center”): an equipment supply agreement for the procurement and supply of MEP equipment (the “Supply Contract”) and an installation works contract for the installation of the MEP equipment and systems (the “Installation Contract” and, together with the Supply Contract, the “Contracts”). The Contracts are in addition to the letters of award for the MEP equipment and installation works for Phase 1A of the Data Center previously announced by the Company on September 1, 2026. The aggregate contract price under the Contracts is in a range between US$60 million and US$65 million, exclusive of Indonesian value-added tax. Each Contract is priced on a fixed lump-sum basis and is subject to adjustment only as provided in the relevant Contract, including for variations instructed by the Indonesian Subsidiary. The contract prices are denominated in U.S. dollars and are payable in Indonesian Rupiah at the Bank Indonesia middle rate on the relevant invoice date. The Contracts provide for delivery of the equipment and completion of the installation works during 2027, in accordance with the milestones set out in the Contracts. Each Contract provides for liquidated damages for delay, subject to a cap, and for a defects notification period following taking-over of the installed works. The Indonesian Subsidiary may terminate either Contract for convenience on notice, subject to payment for work performed and other costs reasonably incurred by the relevant contractor. The Contracts relate to the construction of the Data Center and do not themselves generate revenue. Completion of Phase 1B and commencement of operations at the Data Center remain subject to, among other things, performance by the contractors engaged by the Company and its subsidiaries (the “Group”), completion of related construction and power supply works, availability of funding and applicable regulatory approvals. The Contracts do not by themselves guarantee successful completion of Phase 1B or of the Data Center, or operational capacity, customer utilization, revenue, profitability or positive cash flow. About Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd is a Nasdaq-listed company with two principal business focuses: (i) its established premium whisky operations; and (ii) the development of AI computing infrastructure and cloud-based computing services. These two lines of business represent the Company’s primary operational pillars, with the Company dedicating substantial resources to the development and scaling of its AI computing infrastructure business. The Company’s whisky operations include procurement and distribution of bottled whisky, procurement and distribution of raw cask whisky, and cask-to-bottle and distribution services, including brand-authorized bottling, packaging and sales, in Taiwan and select international markets. Since early 2026, the Company has launched and been developing its AI Computing Infrastructure Initiative through subsidiaries in Singapore, Indonesia and other jurisdictions. This initiative represents a principal business focus, backed by substantive contractual arrangements for commercial AI computing cloud services and the development of supporting data center, power, network and technical infrastructure. The Company’s historical operating revenue has been derived from its whisky operations, and the AI computing business remains in development and deployment and is subject to significant business, financing, construction, technology, regulatory, customer demand and execution risks. artigo.texto: Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery - Collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, building on an initial 200 MWh project award in ERCOT. RALEIGH, N.C. and ARLINGTON, Va., November 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linxon and Fluence Energy, Inc. today announced a strategic collaboration to pursue and deliver battery energy storage system projects through a more integrated OEM-EPC model. The collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise with Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid integration and project execution capabilities. The collaboration has already contributed to securing a 200 MWh battery energy storage project in Texas' ERCOT market. Linxon and Fluence are also jointly pursuing additional opportunities across the energy storage and grid infrastructure markets. Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid connection and complex EPC execution capabilities complement Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise. Together, the companies can address customer requirements spanning the battery energy storage system and the infrastructure required to connect it safely and reliably to the grid. Energy storage projects can separate technology supply, grid connection and EPC execution into distinct scopes, creating technical, commercial and schedule interfaces that must be resolved later in the project lifecycle. Linxon and Fluence intend to address these interfaces earlier by coordinating system requirements, engineering, constructability, procurement, commissioning and project execution from the development stage. By aligning technology, engineering, constructability, procurement, project execution and commissioning from the early stages of a project, Linxon and Fluence aim to reduce interfaces, anticipate risks and create a more competitive and predictable delivery model for customers. From managing interfaces to Engineering the Mission together At the center of the collaboration is a simple principle: align the battery system and grid infrastructure through a coordinated approach to planning, integration, and delivery. The objective is not simply to place two separate scopes alongside each other. It is to align technology, grid integration and project execution earlier, allowing the companies to identify interfaces, improve constructability and establish execution readiness before mobilization. Fluence brings its energy storage technology and expertise, while Linxon brings its EPC system integration and execution capabilities through its Mission Ready EPC approach. The collaboration incorporates Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, which focuses on preparing projects for successful execution before mobilization. Through early readiness planning, interface management, constructability reviews, risk identification, standardization and local capability development, Mission Ready EPC is designed to improve execution readiness and delivery predictability. The companies intend to apply these principles across future opportunities while maintaining the flexibility required to address customer specifications, market conditions and local project requirements. Together, the companies intend to create an integrated framework that can be applied across projects and markets, improving execution consistency while maintaining the flexibility required for specific customer needs. Building competitiveness before execution Earlier collaboration between the Fluence OEM and EPC is expected to create opportunities for standardized interfaces, repeatable engineering, improved constructability and more coordinated procurement and execution planning. The approach is also intended to support the progressive development of the engineering knowledge, training, field competencies and local delivery ecosystems required for future energy storage deployment. For customers, this can support earlier risk identification, clearer accountability and a more coordinated path from technology selection through grid connection and project delivery. "We want to redefine the traditional relationship between an OEM and an EPC," said Nicolas Sanloup, Managing Director Americas at Linxon. "This is not about one company providing technology and another executing around it. It is about engineering the mission together from the beginning. By combining Fluence's technology expertise with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, our ambition is to anticipate interfaces, build competitiveness into the solution and develop local capabilities ahead of demand." "By bringing technology and EPC execution closer together from the outset, we have an opportunity to simplify project delivery and create a scalable and repeatable approach for our customers," said Jeff Monday, SVP and Chief Growth Officer, Fluence. "This collaboration reflects the purpose of Fluence PACE, our newly launched strategic partner program, which formalizes how we work with select partners whose capabilities complement our strengths. Our work with Linxon demonstrates how that model can support customers while creating opportunities for continued growth." A new way to deliver energy infrastructure The Linxon–Fluence collaboration is designed to move the OEM–EPC relationship from a transactional interface toward an integrated delivery ecosystem, combining technology, project integration and execution around a common mission. artigo.texto: Depois de muito vai e vem durante este ano, o governo definiu as datas para realização do leilão de reserva de capacidade de armazenamento. Falta, no entanto, saber se a legislação que trata da remuneração das baterias chegará intacta ao dia 2 de dezembro. A pouco mais de duas semanas da primeira disputa, uma tentativa de alterar uma regra aprovada há menos de um ano pelo próprio Congresso coloca em dúvida o calendário defendido pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME). A controvérsia está no rateio dos custos de contratação das baterias. A Lei 15.269/2025, que se propõe a fazer uma reforma do setor elétrico, determinou que a despesa seja dividida exclusivamente entre os geradores de energia. Mobilizado pelo próprio setor de armazenamento, o deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP) apresentou o PL 3.716/2026 para revogar esse dispositivo e submeter o armazenamento à regra geral da reserva de capacidade, que prevê o custeio pelos consumidores de energia elétrica. A proposta tem apoio de diferentes segmentos da geração, mas enfrenta um problema de calendário. Embora tenha recebido regime de urgência na Câmara, o texto precisaria superar as negociações em torno do relatório, ser aprovado pelos deputados e pelo Senado e seguir para sanção presidencial antes dos leilões para produzir efeitos sobre as regras dos certames. Há quem considere, no meio político, difícil concluir todo esse processo no prazo disponível, principalmente pela possibilidade de a proposta se transformar em um instrumento para reavaliar outros pontos da reforma do setor elétrico. O próprio relator do projeto na Câmara, Danilo Forte (PP-CE), tem um histórico de atuação em assuntos que ficaram pendentes na reforma do setor elétrico. Durante a tramitação da MP 1.304/2025, o parlamentar apresentou uma emenda para ampliar o ressarcimento aos geradores eólicos e solares pelos cortes de geração determinados pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), incluindo restrições associadas à confiabilidade elétrica e limitações de transmissão. Jardim reconheceu publicamente, na última sexta-feira (13/11), que Forte pretende incorporar temas como ressarcimento do curtailment, adicionalidade e descontos pelo uso da rede. O autor da proposta tem defendido um texto mais enxuto justamente para facilitar sua aprovação. O diretor-geral da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), Sandoval Feitosa, já pontuou que uma alteração legislativa exigiria a republicação dos editais e a remarcação do leilão. Como a agência trabalha com um intervalo mínimo de 30 dias entre a publicação dos documentos e a realização dos certames, a mudança praticamente afastaria a possibilidade de realizar os certames ainda em 2026. Além dos prazos, há também uma questão econômica. A alteração do rateio não significa que os leilões perdem automaticamente a atratividade, mas mexe em uma premissa relevante para a estruturação da contratação. A definição de quem paga, como os valores serão arrecadados e quais mecanismos garantirão o fluxo de recursos interfere na avaliação de riscos dos empreendimentos e pode influenciar os preços e as condições de financiamento. Uma mudança às vésperas da disputa exigiria ao menos uma reavaliação dessas condições. A aprovação posterior tampouco resolveria imediatamente o problema. Caso os certames sejam realizados sob a legislação atual e o Congresso altere o rateio antes da assinatura dos contratos, abre-se espaço para uma discussão sobre os efeitos da nova regra sobre um procedimento licitatório já realizado — e um horizonte de insegurança jurídica e regulatória sobre o primeiro leilão de baterias. Judicialização ainda não é consenso A possibilidade de recorrer à Justiça pedindo o adiamento do leilão por conta de uma possível revisão da remuneração já foi discutida por agentes do setor, mas não há consenso sobre a conveniência dessa estratégia. Na Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (Abeeólica), por exemplo, a hipótese de questionar judicialmente os leilões foi aventada, segundo fontes, mas encontrou resistência interna. A avaliação predominante é de que ainda há espaço para uma solução política, especialmente por meio da tramitação do projeto no Congresso. Dois partidos políticos também chegaram a sondar a possibilidade de questionamento da legislação na Justiça, segundo apurou o JOTA. Ainda assim, interlocutores avaliam que o caráter técnico da discussão e o prazo reduzido até dezembro tornam incerta a obtenção de uma eventual decisão cautelar capaz de suspender os certames. A Aneel, por sua vez, sustenta que a ausência de uma regulamentação definitiva do rateio não impede a realização dos leilões. O argumento é que os pagamentos começarão apenas com a entrada em operação dos sistemas, prevista para agosto de 2028. A agência já aprovou os editais e conduziu uma consulta pública específica sobre a metodologia de divisão do encargo entre os geradores, com alternativas que consideram a flexibilidade das usinas e sua contribuição para o atendimento do sistema. A separação da contratação entre armazenamento e outras formas de reserva de capacidade, como as termelétricas contratadas neste ano, deve ser feita apenas em 2026. O MME estabeleceu em portaria o planejamento dos leilões de 2027 a 2029 e passou a prever certames de reserva de capacidade que poderão considerar conjuntamente diferentes tecnologias, incluindo baterias, sistemas hidráulicos de armazenamento, hidrelétricas e termelétricas. artigo.texto: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), a group of 38 mostly high-income countries, brings together data on family life and family policy in its Family Database, which covers its members, EU countries, and some partner countries. One of its indicators is the share of children born outside of marriage, meaning births where the mother was not legally married at the time. The OECD collects these figures from national statistical offices and Eurostat. In 1970, fewer than one in ten children were born outside of marriage in 20 of the 25 countries with data for that year and 2023. The share has risen in all 25 since then — in Spain, it went from 1.4% to 50%. Most countries don’t have long-term figures on how many couples live together unmarried, which makes this indicator one of the few ways to follow that change over decades. I recently updated the chart with the OECD’s release from October 2025. For most countries, the data used to end in 2020 and now goes to 2023, and to 2024 for five of them. Colombia is in the data for the first time, from 1998 onward, and has the highest share of all. In 2023, 87% of births there were to mothers who weren’t married. artigo.texto: FAYETTEVILLE -- The Washington County Quorum Court on Thursday passed a yearlong moratorium on the construction and development of data centers in the county. Justice of the Peace Evelyn Rios Stafford proposed the moratorium to give the county time to update its planning and zoning rules. The ordinance passed through the Washington County's Services Committee in a 9-5 vote with one abstention Nov. 9. The Quorum Court had a similar vote of 9-6 Thursday. The best time for this ordinance is now when there are no data centers proposed for the county, Stafford told the Quorum Court. "If we think data centers are never going to come to Washington County, well, look at Siloam Springs," she said. The Siloam Springs Board of Directors also recently approved a six-month moratorium on building data centers in that city. The ordinance proposing the moratorium came to the board as the city discussed with developers the possibility of building a data center, according to documents obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request. The board voted 5-2 on Nov. 3 to approve the ordinance. During the year the Washington County moratorium is in place, the Quorum Court along with the county's Planning Board and Planning Department will conduct a review "of the potential impacts of Data Centers and whether the County has appropriate processes, resources, infrastructure, and regulations to address such development," according to the ordinance. This could serve to point out other areas of county code that need improvement, such as with creating a noise ordinance or providing the Quorum Court with ideas of how to better ensure the county code can be enforced, Stafford said. "I think it is a great opportunity, while there is no imminent anything coming, that our planning staff, our planning boards look at these things, find out what criteria is necessary, as a sort of stress test for how we would approach this in the future," Justice of the Peace Vladimir Rivera Lopez said. Justice of the Peace Willie Leming said he believes the current, normal permitting processes the county has are enough to properly regulate data centers. "I believe what we got works, and I think this will get us into lawsuits and stuff later on too," he said of the moratorium. Two amendments were made to the ordinance Thursday. One simply corrected some language regarding the day the moratorium would go into effect. The second removed language required the Planning Department to provide reports every 90 days about the potential impacts of data centers. Washington County Planning Director Sam Ata said he worried about being able to meet the deadlines with the department's workload. Stafford proposed striking that portion of the proposed ordinance after hearing from Ata, saying she would trust the Planning Department to get justices of the peace the information they need. The moratorium is scheduled to begin Friday and last 12 months. The next Washington County Quorum Court meeting is scheduled for 6 p.m. Dec. 17 at the Washington County Courthouse. artigo.texto: Gerando resumo A Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica (Abeeólica) ingressou com uma ação civil pública, com pedido de tutela de urgência, para suspender a realização dos leilões de reserva de capacidade (LRCap) para contratação de sistemas de armazenamento por baterias, marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro próximos, bem como os atos destinados à adjudicação, homologação e celebração dos contratos decorrentes do certame. A ação, apresentada na 17ª Vara Federal Cível do Distrito Federal contra a União e a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), questiona a legalidade da realização dos leilões sem a adequada definição do regime de custeio e, adicionalmente, a legitimidade da imposição desse encargo aos geradores de energia. Para a Abeeólica, o trecho da Lei nº 15.269/2025, conhecida como lei de modernização do setor elétrico, que determinou que o custo da contratação das baterias seja pago apenas pelos geradores de energia, ofende a ordem econômica, a isonomia, a legalidade e a segurança jurídica, por isso defende o reconhecimento de sua inconstitucionalidade. “Os leilões não podem ser realizados nas condições atuais. O vício está, antes de tudo, na própria regra que atribui aos geradores o custeio das baterias. O encargo que remunera as baterias tem natureza de preço público, e não de tributo. A consequência relevante dessa natureza é a exigência de nexo entre o custeio e a fruição ou o benefício da utilidade remunerada, o que inexiste no caso. Ao impor o custo a quem não é o beneficiário final, a lei produz transferência injustificada de ônus dos usuários finais aos geradores, por meio de medida desproporcional”, argumenta a ação, que cita que os custos de contratação de reserva de capacidade de maneira geral são arcados pelos usuários finais do sistema. Leia também - Bandeira tarifária em novembro segue verde, sem adicional na conta de luz - Moura estende parceria com chineses e investe R$ 200 milhões em fábrica de PE - Subsídios criam o modelo Robin Hood às avessas e deixam País com sobra de energia e risco de apagão A ação também aponta a existência de vício relacionado à estruturação dos leilões por falta de conclusão da regulamentação que definirá a metodologia de cálculo do montante que cada gerador pagará. “E a minuta da regulamentação em discussão pretende fazer alguns geradores pagarem até quatro vezes mais que outros, por critério que a lei não previu. Ao fazê-lo, a Aneel extrapola a delegação do § 6º e sua competência regulatória (art. 2º da Lei 9.427/1996). Esse vício diz respeito aos próprios leilões e subsistiria ainda que a lei fosse válida", diz. A presidente da Abeeólica, Elbia Gannoum, afirmou ao Estadão/Broadcast que a decisão de judicializar o leilão foi tomada a despeito do avanço de um projeto de lei que visa alterar a lei sobre o custeamento das baterias, em discussão no Congresso Nacional, devido ao prazo limite para entrar com a ação civil pública antes do certame. “Esse prazo limite se esgotou ontem, dia 16, e precisamos entrar com essa ação, e ela, de certa forma, reforça o sinal para o Legislativo resolver logo essa questão legal, porque existe essa ação civil pública e existe uma flagrante inconstitucionalidade nessa cobrança”, afirmou. Ela comentou que a Abeeólica também está preparando uma Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade (Adin) contra o trecho da lei que define os geradores como responsáveis por custear os sistemas de baterias. “A alocação do custo, por essa lei, foi totalmente equivocada, porque a bateria é um recurso que todo o sistema elétrico brasileiro recebe o benefício, o bônus, porém o ônus da bateria foi alocado só para os geradores de energia eólica e solar, então há um problema claríssimo de alocação ineficiente do custo, que o gerador não pode bancar, principalmente num sistema em que está gerando tanto curtailment (cortes de geração)”, disse, salientando que o sinal de investimento ficou deturpado, gerando insegurança entre empreendedores.

artigo.texto: Trinity Capital Inc. Provides $100 Million in Debt Financing to Accelerate Phononic's Growth and Manufacturing Expansion for AI Data Centers PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN), a leading alternative asset manager, today announced the commitment of $100 million in debt financing to Phononic, a North Carolina-based company developing solid-state cooling solutions for AI data centers. The financing will support accelerated growth and manufacturing capacity expansion to meet increasing customer demand. Phononic's proprietary Thermal Control Systems™ provide software-defined cooling for AI infrastructure by combining high-performance thermoelectric devices with intelligent controls. Compact, solid-state devices and an integrated software control layer deliver precision cooling at the point of need for critical components, including GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, networking silicon, and the optical transceivers that connect them. Phononic's Thermal Fabric™ software layer monitors conditions throughout the data center and dynamically adjusts thermal control in real time as AI workloads change. Together, these solutions are designed to unlock greater AI infrastructure performance, optimize compute and facility capacity, and reduce energy and water consumption. "As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important," said Phil Gager, Senior Managing Director of Tech Lending at Trinity Capital. "Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we're pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build." Phononic enters its next phase of growth as a profitable company backed by leading venture and growth-equity investors. With demand accelerating across AI infrastructure, the company is expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer requirements and scale delivery of its intelligent thermal control solutions. "AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale," said Dr. Tony Atti, CEO and Founder of Phononic. "Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure." About Trinity Capital Inc. Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN) is an alternative asset manager that seeks to deliver consistent returns for investors through access to private credit markets. Trinity Capital sources and structures investments in well-capitalized growth-oriented companies across five distinct lending verticals: Tech Lending, Equipment Finance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Sponsor Finance, and Asset Based Lending. As a long-term, trusted partner for innovative companies seeking tailored debt solutions, Trinity Capital has deployed more than $6.8 billion across over 511 investments since inception in 2008 (as of September 30, 2026). Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, Trinity Capital's dedicated team is strategically located across the United States and Europe. For more information on Trinity Capital, please visit trinitycapital.com and stay connected to the latest activity via LinkedIn. About Phononic Phononic is a leader in software-defined thermal control for AI infrastructure, combining breakthrough solid-state cooling technology with intelligent hardware and software to unlock greater performance, efficiency, and reliability. Deployed across major U.S. hyperscalers, Phononic's solutions deliver precision thermal control at the source for optical connectivity, GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, and other critical AI components. Through its Thermal Control Systems™ and Thermal Fabric™ intelligence layer, Phononic enables real-time, workload-responsive thermal optimization that helps mitigate throttling, improve energy efficiency, and maximize AI infrastructure performance. For more information, visit www.phononic.com. artigo.texto: Cirion lança Datrix para operar 12 data centers na América Latina Marca reúne instalações em seis países, incluindo o Brasil, e terá atuação voltada a hyperscalers, provedores de nuvem e aplicações de IA. A Cirion Technologies anunciou hoje (18) o lançamento da Datrix, marca que passa a identificar seu negócio de data centers na América Latina. A operação reúne 12 instalações distribuídas por Brasil, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colômbia e Equador, com foco no atendimento à demanda por infraestrutura de nuvem, IA e computação de alta densidade. A criação da Datrix faz parte da intenção da Cirion em estabelecer uma identidade específica para suas operações de data centers, com liderança dedicada ao segmento. Nelson Fonseca ocupa o cargo de CEO da nova marca, enquanto Santiago Londoño permanece à frente da Cirion Technologies. A estrutura terá como público-alvo hyperscalers, provedores de serviços em nuvem, plataformas de conteúdo e empresas que necessitam de capacidade de processamento e armazenamento de dados em diferentes mercados latino-americanos. Modelo neutro de conectividade A Datrix atuará no modelo carrier-neutral, que permite aos clientes contratar serviços de conectividade de diferentes operadoras e fornecedores de redes. Nesse formato, as empresas instaladas nos data centers podem escolher seus prestadores de telecomunicações de acordo com suas necessidades operacionais. Segundo a Cirion, a nova marca utilizará a infraestrutura e os relacionamentos comerciais desenvolvidos pelo grupo na região para atender clientes atuais e novos. A estratégia contempla o fortalecimento da presença regional e a ampliação das capacidades de infraestrutura destinadas a organizações que buscam estabelecer ou expandir operações na América Latina. “A Datrix dá a essa experiência um foco claro no que vem pela frente: o rápido crescimento da nuvem e da inteligência artificial na América Latina”, afirmou Nelson Fonseca, CEO da Datrix. O lançamento ocorre em um contexto de expansão do setor na América Latina. Segundo dados da CBRE citados pela Cirion, o estoque regional de data centers cresceu 41,3% no primeiro trimestre de 2026, em comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior, registrando a maior taxa de crescimento entre as regiões analisadas. A companhia associa esse movimento ao aumento da demanda por serviços de nuvem e aplicações de inteligência artificial, que exigem infraestrutura de processamento e armazenamento de dados. “O papel da América Latina na economia digital das próximas décadas será definido pela infraestrutura que construímos hoje”, declarou Santiago Londoño, CEO da Cirion Technologies. Com a Datrix, a Cirion passa a concentrar a identidade de suas operações de data centers em uma marca dedicada a esse mercado, mantendo a atuação regional e o modelo de infraestrutura neutra em relação aos fornecedores de conectividade. (Com assessoria de imprensa)

artigo.texto: Exchange Traded Concepts and Kiwoom Securities (USA) Launch KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF (Nasdaq: SDC) The second KICK ETF offers U.S. investors index-based exposure to the data center hardware and space infrastructure companies that may one day support computing in orbit. OKLAHOMA CITY , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC ("ETC") and Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. today announced the launch of the KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF (Nasdaq: SDC), the second fund in the KICK ETFs lineup. SDC joins the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (NYSE Arca: KCHP), which began trading on September 15, 2026. AI is putting growing pressure on power grids. The International Energy Agency projects that global data center electricity demand will more than double by 2030, and grid connections have become a constraint for some new builds.1 That pressure has led some companies to explore whether data centers could one day operate in orbit, where certain orbits could offer near-constant sunlight, radiative cooling and no need for land.2,3 In October 2026, Google launched a prototype satellite carrying its AI chips and reported running an AI model on it in orbit.4,5 Starcloud, a privately held startup, has reported in December 2025 that it has trained an AI model on a GPU in space.6 The concept remains early-stage, with unresolved challenges in launch costs, radiation, maintenance and commercial viability.7 Putting computing in orbit would take more than a satellite. Data center hardware must process, move and store data, and space infrastructure would need to carry and support the equipment. SDC seeks to track, before fees and expenses, the Akros Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ("the Index"), which holds up to 30 U.S.-listed companies across those two areas: data center hardware, including compute, networking and interconnect, and memory and storage; and space infrastructure, including launch, satellites and spacecraft, satellite services and ground equipment. Many of these companies may also serve ground data centers and other markets. Inclusion in the Index does not by itself mean a company operates an orbital data center or earns revenue from one. "Investors are being asked to make sense of AI infrastructure at a time when it is spreading in more directions than ever," said Garrett Stevens, Co-Founder and Chief Business Officer of Exchange Traded Concepts. "We believe they are better served when they know exactly which part of the buildout they own. KCHP offered investors focused access to Korea's semiconductor industry. SDC seeks to apply the same discipline to an earlier-stage frontier: the effort to extend data infrastructure into space." "Most of the conversation about AI infrastructure stays on the ground, with the chips, the power and the buildings," said Yoon Gu Eric Lee, President and Chief Executive Officer of Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. "The companies building the hardware and space systems that could support computing in orbit deserve a place in that conversation. With SDC, U.S. investors can access that segment through a rules-based index in a familiar ETF format." The Index is owned, calculated, administered and published by Akros Technologies, Inc.Akros ranks companies using NEXUS, its proprietary rubric-based framework that evaluates how central each company's business is to the Index theme. An Index committee reviews constituents for continued eligibility. The Index is reconstituted and rebalanced quarterly. The Index treats data center hardware and space infrastructure as separate sleeves and targets 15 companies in each. Each sleeve's share of Index weight is set by its number of constituents at every quarterly rebalance, and within each sleeve, companies are weighted by free-float market capitalization. Holdings and weights shift between rebalances, and current holdings are published daily at kicketfs.com/sdc. SDC seeks to track its Index by holding the stocks in the Index. Investors can buy and sell shares of the Fund through a standard brokerage account. About Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. Founded in 2000, Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. is a Korea-based financial services company offering securities brokerage, investment trading, discretionary investment and advisory services. The company is a core member of the Daou Kiwoom Group and serves investors through its online financial platform. Learn more about the parent company at www.kiwoom.com/h/ir/en/main and the KICK ETFs at www.KICKETFS.com. artigo.texto: Since Gov. Janet Mills vetoed a temporary statewide ban on AI data centers in April, dozens of Maine communities have explored imposing restrictions of their own. At least 30 towns and cities in Maine had taken action on data centers as of Nov. 19, and a few more are weighing it, according to news reports and public notices. Three municipalities — North Berwick, Scarborough and Westbrook— have permanently banned data centers, and more than two dozen others have passed moratoriums. Those temporary bans are typically designed to give local officials time to weigh more permanent policies. While some municipalities have passed bans due to proposed (or rumored) data centers, many others have done so as a precaution. Mills vetoed the temporary statewide ban after lawmakers declined to include an amendment that would have allowed for a data center project at the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay. That proposal was put on pause this summer, but the effort resumed in November. Data center projects have been proposed, or at least publicly explored, in several Maine communities, from Sanford to the ocean off Eastport. Some proposals have been withdrawn in the face of public opposition, such as one in Lewiston. Following the Nov. 3 election — during which a slew of towns’ voters passed data center bans or moratoriums — elected officials have signaled support for revisiting a temporary statewide ban. The following list of municipalities that have passed permanent bans or temporary moratoriums, or are considering action, is derived from reporting by journalists in newsrooms across Maine. It will be updated on a regular basis. Did we miss your city or town? Send information to [email protected]. BANS NORTH BERWICK North Berwick voters approved a permanent ban on data centers in the Nov. 3 election. The ban applies to facilities with an aggregate data center area of at least 25,000 square feet. The Select Board initially explored a moratorium but in June opted to send the issue straight to voters instead. Source: Portland Press Herald SCARBOROUGH The Scarborough Town Council passed a data center ban in November. The ban distinguishes between standalone data centers and accessory spaces, such as server rooms, telecommunications closets and computer equipment rooms.
