artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Reports Third Quarter 2026 Revenue of $44.8 Million, 84% Increase over Prior Year Period Nine Month Revenue Increased 65% and Gross Profit Increased 94%; Company on Track to Deliver First 10 MW of AI Capacity to Customer at Michigan Data Center in December 2026 LAS VEGAS , Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter revenue increased 84% to $44.8 million, from $24.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, and gross profit increased 67% to $10.5 million, from $6.3 million from the prior year period. Revenue growth was driven by the inclusion of Gresham Worldwide, Inc. ("Gresham") following its reconsolidation in November 2025, higher lending and trading revenue, primarily from unrealized gains on equity investments, and stronger crane operations at Circle 8 Crane Services, LLC ("Circle 8"). Financial and Business Highlights - Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 84% to$44.8 million , compared to$24.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. - Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 65% to$123.8 million , compared to$75.2 million in the first nine months of 2025. - Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 94% to$34.3 million , compared to$17.7 million in the first nine months of 2025, and gross margin expanded to 27.7% from 23.5% during the same periods. - Circle 8 revenue increased 26% to $12.2 million for the three months endedSeptember 30, 2026 . - Energy segment operating income, which includes Circle 8, rose to $2.6 million for the three months endedSeptember 30, 2026 from$450,000 in the prior year period, a nearly sixfold increase. - The Company remains on track to energize the first 10 megawatts ("MW") of AI capacity at its Michigan data center inDecember 2026 , with an additional 10 MW targeted by the end ofMarch 2027 . - Subsequent to the quarter end, the Company received $15.0 million in gross proceeds from a convertible note financing and repaid$12.8 million of other convertible notes. "This quarter demonstrates what our operating businesses can contribute as we build out our Michigan AI data center," said Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Circle 8 delivered meaningful growth in both revenue and operating income. Our top priority now is commissioning our initial AI capacity and meeting our commitments to our customer, while keeping close attention on expenses and the capital required to complete our planned development." As previously announced, the Company will host a conference call November 23, 2026, at 2:30 p.m. Pacific Time to discuss these results, followed by a broader discussion of its businesses, operating developments and strategic priorities as part of its Investor Day. All stockholders, investors and other interested parties are invited to participate and are encouraged to register using the following link: Webinar Registration - Zoom Michigan AI Data Center Development Through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Alliance Cloud Services, LLC, the Company is developing approximately 20 MW of critical AI compute capacity at its data center campus in Dowagiac, Michigan, under a master services agreement with a California-based neocloud customer. The Company ceased Bitcoin mining at the Michigan data center on September 1, 2026 for the transition to AI infrastructure services. The agreement has an initial term of 10 years, with two five-year extension options exercisable by the customer. If the customer exercises both options and the Company meets its obligations under the agreement, the initial 20 MW deployment represents total contract value of approximately $1.2 billion over the resulting 20-year term. The customer also holds a right of first offer, exercisable within two years of the agreement's execution, on an additional 32 MW of capacity. If the customer exercises that right and both extension options, the total contract value would increase to approximately $3.0 billion. The Company's current development targets are December 2026 for the first 10 MW and the end of March 2027 for the additional 10 MW. The schedule remains subject to financing availability, construction progress, equipment procurement, commissioning and customer deployment requirements. While gross profit increased, higher operating expenses resulted in larger operating losses in the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter 2026 operating expenses were $29.9 million, compared to $20.3 million in the prior year period, primarily reflecting higher compensation, consulting and professional fees and the inclusion of Gresham. The third quarter 2026 net loss narrowed to $13.0 million from $13.6 million in the prior year period, benefiting from gains of approximately $9.2 million from changes in the fair value of crypto assets and $4.0 million from changes in the fair value of embedded derivative liabilities. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $18.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $15.3 million in the prior year period, reflecting higher preferred dividends, including $2.3 million representing the fair value of Class B common stock distributed to holders of convertible preferred stock. The nine-month net loss also reflected significant non-cash items, principally depreciation and amortization of $18.7 million, amortization of debt discount of $6.6 million and a $4.1 million non-cash change in the participation liability, partially offset by $12.0 million of crypto asset mining revenue received in Bitcoin and a $6.2 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of embedded derivative liabilities. artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data, Inc. Announces Intent to Launch Previously Announced Exchange Offer on or about November 20, 2026 LAS VEGAS , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that it intends to commence its previously announced exchange offer to purchase up to 192,308,000 shares of its Class A Common Stock, $0.001 par value per share ("Common Stock") in exchange for units (the "Units") consisting of (a) $2.00 in cash and (b) one share of preferred stock with a stated value of $24.00 per share (the "Preferred Stock"), per 100 shares of Common Stock on or about November 20, 2026. The Company previously announced that it anticipated formally launching the exchange offer on or around November 17, 2026. Due to the recent global outages of various enterprise services, the Company is now anticipating formally launching the exchange offer on or about November 20, 2026, subject to board approval, regulatory approval and customary closing conditions. Details regarding the proposed exchange offer and instructions for stockholders interested in participating will be provided in the Offer to Exchange and related documents, which will be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") and distributed to the Company stockholders. The exchange offer will not be made to any person in any jurisdiction in which either the exchange offer, or solicitation or sale thereof, is unlawful. This press release is for informational purposes only and shall not constitute an offer to buy or sell Common Stock or any other securities. Any solicitation of offers to buy the Common Stock will only be made pursuant to an Offer to Exchange and related materials to be sent to the Company stockholders on the commencement of the exchange offer. Company stockholders should read such materials carefully when they become available because they will contain important information, including the terms and conditions of the proposed exchange offer. The tender offer documents will be available without charge at the SEC's website at http://www.sec.gov and will be delivered without charge to all stockholders of the Company who so request it. It is anticipated that the exchange offer will be made pursuant to the exemption from registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, contained in Section 3(a)(9) thereof. Under that exemption, if Common Stock exchanged is freely tradeable, the Preferred Stock received in exchange therefor will be freely tradeable. If the Common Stock is restricted, the Preferred Stock will be restricted to the same degree. For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov. About Hyperscale Data, Inc. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors. Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141. On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture. Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems at the site in a fully Tier III environment, creating advanced, enterprise-grade infrastructure to run demanding AI applications at scale. Deployment is underway. The agreement provides Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems and gives Argentum's customers a faster path to high-performance inference capacity. "Partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for Argentum AI," said Andrew Sobko, Founder & CEO, Argentum AI. "This agreement reflects our shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale." "Our agreement gives us a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way, this coupled with our mission-critical capabilities, decades of operational and services experience will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers," said Jamie Rutledge, President, Kyndryl U.S. The facility welcomes a fast-growing, enterprise-grade AI inference company, whose technology powers some of the world's most widely used AI applications, as its flagship anchor tenant. Argentum AI and Kyndryl intend to broaden their collaboration to support Argentum's growth and evolving mission-critical enterprise AI infrastructure needs. About Argentum AI Argentum AI is a premium GPU cloud provider. The company originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, delivering dedicated bare metal GPU capacity to AI model builders, inference providers and enterprises. Argentum works with data center operators and builds capacity around customer demand, with a focus on speed of delivery, reliability and long-term partnerships. artigo.texto: Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery - Collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, building on an initial 200 MWh project award in ERCOT. RALEIGH, N.C. and ARLINGTON, Va., November 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linxon and Fluence Energy, Inc. today announced a strategic collaboration to pursue and deliver battery energy storage system projects through a more integrated OEM-EPC model. The collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise with Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid integration and project execution capabilities. The collaboration has already contributed to securing a 200 MWh battery energy storage project in Texas'ERCOT market. Linxon and Fluence are also jointly pursuing additional opportunities across the energy storage and grid infrastructure markets. Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid connection and complex EPC execution capabilities complement Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise. Together, the companies can address customer requirements spanning the battery energy storage system and the infrastructure required to connect it safely and reliably to the grid. Energy storage projects can separate technology supply, grid connection and EPC execution into distinct scopes, creating technical, commercial and schedule interfaces that must be resolved later in the project lifecycle. Linxon and Fluence intend to address these interfaces earlier by coordinating system requirements, engineering, constructability, procurement, commissioning and project execution from the development stage. By aligning technology, engineering, constructability, procurement, project execution and commissioning from the early stages of a project, Linxon and Fluence aim to reduce interfaces, anticipate risks and create a more competitive and predictable delivery model for customers. From managing interfaces to Engineering the Mission together At the center of the collaboration is a simple principle: align the battery system and grid infrastructure through a coordinated approach to planning, integration, and delivery. The objective is not simply to place two separate scopes alongside each other. It is to align technology, grid integration and project execution earlier, allowing the companies to identify interfaces, improve constructability and establish execution readiness before mobilization. Fluence brings its energy storage technology and expertise, while Linxon brings its EPC system integration and execution capabilities through its Mission Ready EPC approach. The collaboration incorporates Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, which focuses on preparing projects for successful execution before mobilization. Through early readiness planning, interface management, constructability reviews, risk identification, standardization and local capability development, Mission Ready EPC is designed to improve execution readiness and delivery predictability. The companies intend to apply these principles across future opportunities while maintaining the flexibility required to address customer specifications, market conditions and local project requirements. Together, the companies intend to create an integrated framework that can be applied across projects and markets, improving execution consistency while maintaining the flexibility required for specific customer needs. Building competitiveness before execution Earlier collaboration between the Fluence OEM and EPC is expected to create opportunities for standardized interfaces, repeatable engineering, improved constructability and more coordinated procurement and execution planning. The approach is also intended to support the progressive development of the engineering knowledge, training, field competencies and local delivery ecosystems required for future energy storage deployment. For customers, this can support earlier risk identification, clearer accountability and a more coordinated path from technology selection through grid connection and project delivery. "We want to redefine the traditional relationship between an OEM and an EPC," said Nicolas Sanloup, Managing Director Americas at Linxon . "This is not about one company providing technology and another executing around it. It is about engineering the mission together from the beginning. By combining Fluence's technology expertise with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, our ambition is to anticipate interfaces, build competitiveness into the solution and develop local capabilities ahead of demand." "By bringing technology and EPC execution closer together from the outset, we have an opportunity to simplify project delivery and create a scalable and repeatable approach for our customers," said Jeff Monday, SVP and Chief Growth Officer, Fluence . "This collaboration reflects the purpose of Fluence PACE, our newly launched strategic partner program, which formalizes how we work with select partners whose capabilities complement our strengths. Our work with Linxon demonstrates how that model can support customers while creating opportunities for continued growth." A new way to deliver energy infrastructure The Linxon–Fluence collaboration is designed to move the OEM–EPC relationship from a transactional interface toward an integrated delivery ecosystem, combining technology, project integration and execution around a common mission. For customers, the ambition is clear: fewer interfaces, earlier alignment, greater competitiveness and more predictable execution. One technology strategy. One execution strategy. One mission. artigo.texto: RS offers ebm-papst solutions for rack-level thermal challenges in high-density data centers ebm-papst DiaForce, AxiForce, and RadiCal series fans help mitigate rack-level hot spots, minimize harmonic vibration, reduce parasitic power draw, and improve energy efficiency in critical data center infrastructure. FORT WORTH, Texas , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RS, a high-service global product and service solutions provider for industrial customers, offers high-performance ebm-papst air-moving products engineered to solve rack-level thermal management challenges in high-density data centers, including several series of robust, compact, and versatile fans. As processing demands soar, these proven fan technologies allow data center operators, system builders, and thermal engineers to optimize airflow, overcome high static pressure resistance, minimize harmonic vibration, reduce parasitic power draw, and reliably protect critical assets from thermal damage and mechanical stress. Rapid growth in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and high-performance computing has pushed server rack power densities from 3–5kW a decade ago to 40–100kW or more per rack today. Because server chips convert nearly all electrical energy into heat, unmitigated thermal energy creates localized hot spots that facility-level air conditioning cannot effectively dissipate, risking component degradation, silicon melting, and unplanned downtime that averages around $9,000 per minute. While liquid cooling adoption is growing, fan-based forced-air cooling remains the global standard for roughly 90% of data centers due to lower capital costs, easier maintenance, legacy facility compatibility, and zero risk of fluid leaks near high-voltage electronics. Effectively cooling these densely populated server chassis requires specialized fans engineered to overcome extreme aerodynamic resistance from PCBs, power supplies, and cabling without introducing excessive noise, harmonic vibration, or energy penalties. ebm-papst offers a variety of precision engineered fans through RS that directly resolve these common rack-level thermal and mechanical constraints. Key product lines include: - DiaForce series diagonal compact fans: Designed to combine the high volumetric airflow of axial fans with the high static pressure capabilities of centrifugal blowers, these single-stage units deliver up to 50% higher air performance than single-stage axial fans with static pressure matching traditional counter-rotating units. Their unique single-motor diagonal design cuts motor count in half compared to dual-motor counter-rotating setups, significantly reducing the harmonic vibration energy that causes hard drive read/write errors while lowering acoustic noise by 6–12 dB(A) with superior tonality. Available in standard 40mm, 80mm, and 120mm footprints, DiaForce fans provide high-efficiency cooling for high-density server chassis and uninterruptible power supply systems. - AxiForce series compact axial fans: Engineered specifically for high-static-pressure server rack environments, these compact axial fans feature optimized blade aerodynamics, lower noise profiles, reduced electrical power draw, and robust environmental construction compared to legacy axial designs. They are available in compact frame sizes ranging from 40mm to 200mm, directly corresponding to vertical rack unit (U) heights from 1U chassis (40mm) up to 4U and larger enclosures (120mm and 172mm). This structural alignment enables reliable, space-efficient thermal protection across server chassis, power supplies, and rack enclosures. - RadiCal series AC and EC centrifugal fans: Featuring backward-curved impellers from 190mm to 250mm with aerodynamically shaped blades, these centrifugal fans minimize energy losses, flow separation, and turbulence to achieve maximum aerodynamic efficiency. Available with GreenTech EC motor technology and variable speed controls, they reduce energy consumption by up to 50% compared to traditional AC alternatives to curb facility-wide parasitic power draw. Their high-volume airflow capabilities make them ideal for computer room air conditioners, air handling units, supply fan grids, rear-door heat exchangers, and in-row cooling architectures. "As data centers scale to handle generative AI and high-performance computing, thermal management has shifted from a facility-wide consideration to a precise, component-level engineering discipline," said Steve Berestecky, Director of Information Technology & Clean Room Air Technologies at ebm-papst. "Evaluating fans strictly on total volumetric airflow is no longer sufficient when dense internal components create intense aerodynamic impedance. By matching static pressure requirements, optimizing air velocity at critical component sites, and utilizing intelligent PWM control loops, ebm-papst solutions like our DiaForce, AxiForce, and RadiCal series fans allow engineers to master thermal density, curb parasitic power consumption, and protect operational uptime." To learn more about high-performance ebm-papst air-moving products available through RS, visit the links embedded here and check out the new RS Expert Advice article, "High-density rack-level data center cooling," featuring Steve Berestecky. For assistance identifying, procuring, deploying, and maintaining ebm-papst products engineered to optimize data center server rack cooling and maximize uptime, please contact your local RS representative at 1.866.433.5722 or reach out to the RS technical solutions team. artigo.texto: Solenis and Vertiv Partner to Advance Liquid Cooling Management for AI Data Centers Strategic partnership combines thermal infrastructure and fluid management expertise while preserving customer choice and flexibility WILMINGTON, Del. , Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Solenis, a leading global provider of fluid and water management solutions, today announced a strategic partnership with Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global leader in critical digital infrastructure, to help data center operators manage the performance and reliability of liquid cooling systems. As AI workloads increase computing density, liquid cooling performance depends on both the cooling infrastructure and the quality of the fluids circulating through it. Managing these elements together can help operators reduce operational risk, protect equipment and improve efficiency. The partnership brings together Vertiv's cooling infrastructure, Next Predict predictive maintenance capabilities and global service scale with Solenis' expertise in fluid chemistry, cooling water management, OnGuard™ water and glycol monitoring systems, and expert-led services. Together, the companies will support customers globally, from system commissioning through ongoing operation and optimization. "Reliable liquid cooling requires more than advanced equipment. Fluid chemistry and the cooling infrastructure must work together to deliver consistent performance," said Mike Howdeshell, President of Solenis' Light Industrial Solutions business. "Our partnership with Vertiv brings complementary expertise to customers while giving them the flexibility to select the solutions that best fit their operational, financial and environmental needs." Key areas of the partnership include: - Fluid health: chemistry management and fluid monitoring to address contamination and corrosion risks. - Operational insight: Solenis OnGuard™ monitoring systems for continuous analysis and identification of potential challenges. - Lifecycle performance: ongoing service and optimization to support critical system reliability and asset protection. Solenis' combination with Chem-Aqua has given the company the scale to offer a broad portfolio of data center solutions, backed by deep domain expertise. Today, Solenis serves more than 500 data centers globally. The partnership with Vertiv is part of Solenis' broader strategy to expand its capabilities in the growing AI data center market through collaboration with industry technology leaders. Together, the companies aim to give customers greater choice and flexibility in managing their cooling infrastructure, while supporting long-term reliability and operational efficiency. About Solenis Solenis is a leading global provider of water treatment, process and hygiene solutions. The company's portfolio includes water treatment chemistries, process aids, functional additives, cleaners, disinfectants and monitoring, control and delivery systems. These technologies help customers improve efficiency, protect assets and reduce environmental impact. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, Solenis has 78 manufacturing facilities and more than 23,000 employees in over 160 countries across six continents. Solenis is a 2026 Best Managed Company Gold Standard honoree. For additional information about Solenis, please visit www.solenis.com or follow us on social media. About Vertiv: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers' vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today's data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, visit Vertiv.com. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that its Board of Directors (the "Board") has declared a monthly cash dividend of $0.2708333 per share of the Company's outstanding 13.00% Series D Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock. Link to NYSE quote for the Company's 13.00% Series D Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock: https://www.nyse.com/quote/XASE:GPUSpD The Company also announced today that the Board has declared a monthly cash dividend of $0.20833 per share of the Company's outstanding 10.00% Series E Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock. The record date for both dividends is November 30, 2026, and the payment date is Thursday, December 10, 2026. For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors, and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov. About Hyperscale Data, Inc. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors. Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141. On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture. artigo.texto: Long-duration energy storage (LDES) companies are attracting investment as utilities, renewable energy developers and data-centre operators seek electricity storage lasting eight to 100 hours. Form Energy, ESS Tech, Energy Dome, Highview Power, Hydrostor, Eos Energy, Invinity Energy Systems, Sumitomo Electric, Sage Geosystems and Malta are competing with iron-air, flow batteries, zinc batteries, compressed air, liquid air, geothermal and thermal storage technologies. The long-duration energy storage industry is expanding beyond conventional lithium-ion batteries as electricity grids require additional flexibility to accommodate solar and wind generation. Unlike shorter-duration batteries, LDES technologies target extended discharge periods, potentially reducing dependence on fossil-fuel generation during prolonged renewable energy shortfalls. However, the market faces major commercial challenges, including high capital expenditure, limited operating references, project financing, efficiency losses and uncertain customer demand. According to Sightline Climate’s H1 2026 energy storage leaderboard, 23 vendors were assessed on technology, financing, deployment progress and capital economics. Tesla and Chint Power led the overall assessment. Among non-lithium providers, Energy Dome ranked third with 78 points, followed by Highview Power with 65, Hydrostor with 63, ESS Tech with 58 and Sage Geosystems with 57. The leaderboard uses an eight-hour threshold for LDES. Its scores are screening indicators, not independent guarantees of profitability or operational performance. 1. Form Energy: 100-Hour Iron-Air Batteries and $750 Million Funding Form Energy develops iron-air batteries designed to discharge electricity for approximately 100 hours. The company reports testing more than 34,700 sub-scale cells, 6,200 full-scale cells and 170 modules. Its approximately 800 MW / 80 GWh agreement pipeline includes a proposed 300 MW / 30 GWh Xcel Energy–Google project and a 10 MW / 1,000 MWh FuturEnergy Ireland project. Form Energy raised $750 million through Series G financing and secured a $270 million credit facility. The combined $1.02 billion financing commitments demonstrate access to capital but do not represent project revenue or commissioned capacity. Manufacturing scale, project delivery and independently verified efficiency remain critical investment tests. 2. ESS Tech: Iron Flow Batteries and 500 MWh Framework ESS Tech develops aqueous iron-flow batteries through its Energy Base platform and is also developing sodium-ion technology under Bridge. A non-binding Juniper framework covers at least 500 MWh, including a proposed 10 MW / 80 MWh project in California. An 8.5 GWh letter of intent involving Alsym represents a potential opportunity, not confirmed equipment sales. Iron-flow batteries offer an alternative to lithium-based systems, but commercial performance depends on manufacturing costs, operating efficiency, equipment reliability and customer orders. Investors should distinguish signed purchase contracts from non-binding agreements and assess liquidity, warranty liabilities and operating cash flow. 3. Energy Dome: 200 MWh Operating CO₂ Battery and Ireland Expansion Energy Dome stores electricity through a carbon dioxide compression and expansion process. Its 20 MW / 200 MWh Sardinia installation provides ten hours of rated storage duration and an operating commercial reference. The company is also developing a 23 MW / 200 MWh project in Ireland, supported by a ten-year capacity contract, with operation targeted for 2028. In India, NTPC has identified an 18 MW / 144 MWh CO₂ battery project at Kudgi. The Indian project represents eight hours of storage duration. Energy Dome’s operating reference strengthens its commercial position, but future growth depends on construction costs, project financing, repeat orders and actual operating efficiency. 4. Highview Power: Liquid-Air Storage and 3.2 GWh Project Opportunity Highview Power develops liquid-air energy storage systems that liquefy air during charging and expand it through turbines to generate electricity. Its Carrington project is rated at 50 MW / 300 MWh, equivalent to six hours. Consequently, Carrington falls below Sightline Climate’s eight-hour LDES threshold, despite being relevant to longer-duration storage. Highview’s proposed 3.2 GWh Hunterston development represents a larger opportunity. However, proposed capacity is not equivalent to an operational installation. Investors should examine financing, construction schedules, equipment efficiency, turbine maintenance and the cost of replicating projects at additional locations. 5. Hydrostor: 5.6 GWh Compressed-Air Storage Pipeline Hydrostor develops advanced compressed-air energy storage using underground storage formations and captured thermal energy. Its planned Silver City project in Australia is rated at 200 MW / 1,600 MWh. The Willow Rock project in California is designed for 500 MW / 4,000 MWh. Together, the two projects represent 700 MW / 5,600 MWh of proposed capacity. Both have eight-hour rated duration, but neither should be classified as an operating project. Hydrostor’s commercial risks include geological suitability, underground engineering, permitting, financing and construction execution. 6. Eos Energy: Revenue Rises 171% to $82.7 Million Eos Energy manufactures aqueous zinc-based stationary batteries. The company reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $82.7 million, increasing 171 percent year over year. Gross margin remained negative at 53 percent, although it improved by 58 percentage points. Adjusted EBITDA margin was negative 77 percent, improving by 96 percentage points. Eos reported a $765 million backlog representing approximately 3.2 GWh and $344.1 million in cash, including restricted cash. artigo.texto: Google bets on superhot geothermal to power Oregon data centers The geothermal startup Quaise Energy has landed a major first customer for its novel, superhot project in central Oregon. On Tuesday, the Houston-based firm announced that Google has agreed to buy 50 megawatts of carbon-free power from Quaise’s first commercial project, called Project Obsidian, near the Newberry Volcano. Quaise will deploy advanced drilling techniques and unique rock-melting technology to access significantly hotter geothermal resources than traditional plants can. Google said it plans to use the energy to help run its existing data center operations in northwest Oregon as early as 2030. The deal is valued at more than $500 million, Quaise confirmed. The startup is working to find offtakers for an additional 200 MW in future capacity at the Oregon site. “We started Quaise to make the Earth’s most abundant energy source universally accessible — and this agreement marks a critical next step, not just for Quaise but for the entire clean energy sector,” Carlos Araque, Quaise’s CEO and president, said in a Tuesday statement. Quaise is one of at least four U.S. geothermal companies to land agreements with tech giants to pursue next-generation plants. Fervo Energy, the startup that’s furthest along in project development, recently inked a landmark deal to supply Google with nearly 400 MW of clean electricity from the Cape Station facility in southwest Utah. Sage Geosystems and XGS Energy are both partnering with Meta to develop facilities in Nevada and New Mexico, respectively. Tech firms are seeking to secure sources of clean, around-the-clock power for their vast buildout of data centers. For geothermal startups, winning customer contracts like these is an essential step toward raising the financing they need to build first-of-a-kind facilities. Their technologies, while promising, have yet to be deployed widely at commercial scales — and questions remain about how effectively they’ll be able to operate over long periods of time. Google is investing in other nascent technologies, too, including long-duration energy storage and advanced nuclear power. “The scale of power that we’re looking for and also the scale of impact we’re trying to have on the grid requires us to foster that ecosystem,” Lucia Tian, who leads Google’s advanced energy technologies team, told the Wall Street Journal. Quaise said its Oregon project will cost about $350 million to build. The company raised $180 million in equity financing in August, which included investment from the oil-and-gas drilling firm Nabors Industries. (Another startup, Mazama Energy, recently nabbed $135 million to accelerate its own superhot geothermal project near the Newberry Volcano.) At the Project Obsidian site, Quaise will initially use oil-and-gas drilling technologies to develop an enhanced geothermal system. The emerging approach involves fracturing rocks and pumping them full of water to create artificial reservoirs. Surrounding rocks heat the water, which is used to drive turbines on the surface to produce power. Fervo is deploying this method at Cape Station, which began selling power from an initial 33-MW unit in September — becoming the first utility-scale, next-gen geothermal facility to hit such a milestone worldwide. Quaise’s goal is to go deeper and hotter. After using conventional tools to drill down some 2.5 miles, the company plans to switch to its millimeter-wave drilling techniques, which involve deploying high-frequency beams that melt and vaporize rocks. Quaise aims to tap into superhot rock, with temperatures above 572 degrees Fahrenheit, to derive more energy from a relatively smaller number of wells. The startup is still testing the unique technology it plans to deploy for the Google-backed power plant. Quaise said it drilled through more than 330 feet of granite at its field site in central Texas last year, and is now working to reach down over 3,200 feet, or about 0.6 mile, at the same site. Maria Gallucci is a senior reporter at Canary Media. She covers emerging clean energy technologies and efforts to electrify transportation and decarbonize heavy industry.

artigo.texto: The company announced the development on November 19, following the signing of the direct power purchase agreement (DPPA) with Vietnam–Singapore Industrial Park (VSIP) in September 2025. Under the agreement, electricity generated from VSIP's rooftop solar panels and integrated battery energy storage system (BESS) is delivered directly to the factory through a dedicated transmission line. The battery stores surplus electricity when solar generation exceeds demand and releases it when needed, helping balance electricity supply and consumption. Together with the factory's existing 12,400 rooftop solar panels, the system is expected to meet approximately 75 per cent of the facility's total electricity demand during the first five years of operation. According to the company, the combined renewable energy system is projected to avoid approximately 20,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) emissions annually, based on Vietnam's grid emission factor of 0.561 tonnes of CO2e per MWh. LEGO Manufacturing Vietnam is exploring additional power purchase agreements to cover the remaining 25 per cent of its electricity demand. Jesper Hassellund Mikkelsen, senior vice president of Asia Operations and general manager of LEGO Manufacturing Vietnam, said the project reflected the role of technology and cooperation in expanding renewable energy use in manufacturing. “By bringing together innovative technology and strong collaboration with our partners, we are turning our renewable energy ambitions into reality and demonstrating what is possible when industry works together,” he said. Nguyen Phu Thinh, general director of VSIP, said the agreement demonstrated how industrial park developers and manufacturers could cooperate on renewable energy projects. “The DPPA between the LEGO Group and VSIP is not only a significant milestone for both organisations, but also a powerful testament to how industrial developers and manufacturers can jointly create a new paradigm for sustainable manufacturing,” Thinh said. The LEGO Group's Vietnam factory began operations in April 2025 as part of the Danish toy maker's expansion in the region. The battery storage system forms part of the factory's renewable electricity supply arrangements, alongside its existing rooftop solar installation.

artigo.texto: A Smiths Group plc (LSE:SMIN) reportou um aumento de 6,1% na receita para o trimestre encerrado em 31 de outubro de 2026, impulsionado pela aquisição da DRC, embora a receita orgânica tenha permanecido inalterada devido à crise no Oriente Médio que afetou sua divisão John Crane. O grupo de engenharia britânico afirmou que a DRC contribuiu com 5,6 pontos percentuais para o crescimento da receita reportada durante o trimestre, beneficiando-se da demanda associada à expansão de data centers. O desempenho variou entre as operações do grupo, com o crescimento nas atividades de construção e aeroespaciais da Flex-Tek sendo compensado pela queda na receita da John Crane e da Thermal Solutions. A receita da John Crane cai 3% em meio à crise no Oriente Médio A John Crane reportou uma queda de 3% na receita orgânica durante o primeiro trimestre, refletindo a contínua interrupção das atividades comerciais e da entrada de pedidos no Oriente Médio. O crescimento nas Américas compensou parcialmente a fraqueza regional, enquanto a entrada de pedidos permaneceu forte em todos os mercados fora do Oriente Médio e da África. A divisão manteve um forte índice de pedidos em relação ao faturamento, indicando que os pedidos recebidos excederam a receita reconhecida durante o período. A Smiths afirmou que a carteira de encomendas continuava a proporcionar visibilidade sobre a atividade futura, embora as condições comerciais no Oriente Médio permanecessem uma restrição ao desempenho a curto prazo. A receita orgânica da Flex-Tek aumenta 3,9% A Flex-Tek apresentou um crescimento orgânico de receita de 3,9%, impulsionado pelos seus negócios de construção e aeroespacial. A operação de construção registrou um crescimento de receita de um dígito alto, beneficiando-se de novos contratos com clientes e iniciativas de preços, apesar das condições ainda desfavoráveis no mercado imobiliário residencial dos EUA. O setor aeroespacial também registrou crescimento, impulsionado pela execução de pedidos existentes e pelas contribuições das renovações de contratos de longo prazo garantidas durante o exercício financeiro anterior. Na divisão de Soluções Térmicas, a receita diminuiu após a conclusão de um grande projeto de aquecimento de altíssima temperatura que havia contribuído para o resultado do período comparativo do ano anterior. Entretanto, a DRC continuou a beneficiar-se do investimento em infraestrutura de centros de dados, contribuindo para o aumento da receita reportada pelo grupo. A meta de margem operacional foi mantida em aproximadamente 21% O Grupo Smiths reiterou sua meta de alcançar uma margem de lucro operacional de aproximadamente 21%. A empresa espera que a rentabilidade se beneficie da alavancagem operacional, do seu Plano de Aceleração e das reduções de custos proporcionadas pelo programa Smiths Excellence. O investimento em iniciativas de crescimento estratégico continua em conjunto com medidas destinadas a melhorar a eficiência operacional. O diretor executivo, Roland Carter, afirmou que a empresa espera que o crescimento orgânico da receita acelere durante o restante do ano fiscal, impulsionado pela carteira de pedidos existente e pelas iniciativas comerciais em andamento. Ele também destacou o crescimento dos negócios de construção e aeroespacial da Flex-Tek, bem como a demanda pelos produtos da DRC por parte de clientes de data centers. Progresso nos planos de descarte de amianto e pagamento de dívidas de empresas A Smiths confirmou que seu plano de desinvestimento da divisão de amianto da John Crane, nos EUA, está progredindo. O grupo também está se preparando para quitar um título de € 650 milhões com vencimento previsto para fevereiro de 2027. A administração manteve suas expectativas de melhoria no crescimento orgânico da receita ao longo do ano fiscal, com o desempenho dependendo da execução contínua de sua carteira de pedidos, das iniciativas de crescimento e das condições comerciais em seus mercados de atuação. artigo.texto: DeKalb County Sets Proactive Rules for Future Data Centers DeKalb Co., Ind. (WPTA) - DeKalb County leaders are taking a “safety first” approach to big tech, passing a new ordinance that sets strict rules for data centers before a single project is even proposed. The new rules spell out exactly where these facilities can operate and what requirements they must meet for water, electricity, and noise. DeKalb County commissioner Kellen Dooley emphasized that this vote was about creating a countywide framework, not approving a specific project. “We’ve not been approached by any data centers at this time,” Dooley said. “Like I said, we want to be proactive on it.” One of the biggest concerns for residents in rural communities is the massive amount of water data centers often require for cooling. Under the new proposal, any future applicant must prove there is enough water available to run the facility without harming existing users. To ensure transparency, the ordinance requires data centers to connect to a municipal water source, such as the cities of Auburn, Garrett, or Butler. “If you go into a municipal water source, then they would be public information that anybody can pull at any time,” Dooley explained, noting that this move makes water usage data accessible to the public. The ordinance also protects the local power grid. If a data center draws its electricity from public utilities, the company, not the taxpayers, must pay for any upgrades needed to support the project. Beyond utilities, the county is also tackling the daily impact on neighbors. The proposal sets strict limits on noise at the property line and requires motion-sensor lighting to reduce light pollution on neighboring properties. To set these standards, leaders consulted with experts as far away as Las Vegas and Canada to understand how vibrations and constant humming can affect the surrounding soil and environment. “We put a baseline in there, so then that we have at the property line value is when we’re going to have exactly what that noise ordinance would be,” Dooley said. For residents like Matt Malott in Garrett, the proactive move brings a sense of relief. Malott said he left feeling much more confident about the future of the county. “I feel a lot better because they’re pre-planning for it, rather than just the data center coming with no rules and regulations, and doing whatever they want,” he said. “There’s a set boundary now, and it feels a lot better than having nothing.” With these rules now in place, DeKalb County is ready for the future, ensuring that any “progress” comes with protections for the people who live there. artigo.texto: A Abeeólica (Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias) pediu à Justiça Federal uma liminar para suspender os primeiros leilões de armazenamento de energia em baterias do país, previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro. A entidade, que representa a indústria nacional de geração eólica, protocolou na 2ª feira (16.nov.2026) uma Ação Civil Pública para impedir a realização do certame até que sejam definidas as regras sobre quem pagará pela contratação dos sistemas e como as despesas serão divididas. A duas semanas da disputa, a associação argumenta que é inconstitucional o trecho da lei que determina que somente os geradores arquem com os custos das baterias. Também contesta a proposta da Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) para distribuir as despesas entre as diferentes fontes de geração. O processo questiona os critérios de rateio sugeridos pela agência, com participação entre 25% e 100%, conforme a flexibilidade de cada fonte. Pelo modelo, geradores eólicos, solares e nucleares pagariam mais; as usinas térmicas teriam custos intermediários, e as hidrelétricas arcariam com as menores parcelas. Para a Abeeólica, algumas empresas poderiam pagar até 4 vezes mais que outras, sem critérios jurídicos claros. As regras de divisão das despesas foram submetidas pela Aneel a consulta pública, mas ainda não receberam aprovação definitiva. A entidade afirma que, sem regulamentação concluída, os agentes de geração não conseguem calcular os riscos e os impactos econômicos antes de apresentar ofertas. A ação, protocolada na 17ª Vara Federal Cível do Distrito Federal, pede a interrupção de todas as fases do certame, da disputa à adjudicação, homologação e assinatura dos contratos. A associação sustenta que as baterias devem reforçar a segurança e a estabilidade de todo o sistema elétrico nacional, beneficiando diretamente os consumidores conectados à rede. Por isso, argumenta que deixar a conta exclusivamente com os geradores viola princípios de isonomia, livre concorrência e segurança jurídica. A controvérsia envolve a Lei 15.269 de 2025, que atribuiu aos geradores os custos da contratação. Nos leilões tradicionais de reserva de capacidade, a cobrança é feita de todos os consumidores finais. Para a Abeeólica, as baterias deveriam seguir essa regra, pois também se destinam a garantir potência ao sistema. A ação cita estimativas do TCU (Tribunal de Contas da União) de que os contratos do leilão podem totalizar de R$ 108 a R$ 153 bilhões. No Congresso, há discussões para mudar a lei e retirar dos geradores a obrigação exclusiva de custear os sistemas. Em 13 de outubro, a Câmara aprovou urgência para o PL (Projeto de Lei) 3.716 de 2026, apresentado pelo deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP) e relatado pelo deputado Danilo Forte (PP-CE). A proposta revoga o trecho da lei de 2025 e prevê a aplicação da regra geral de divisão dos custos. Segundo a Aneel, se o texto for aprovado antes do leilão, será necessário alterar o edital: as despesas passariam a ser compartilhadas pelos usuários finais do SIN (Sistema Interligado Nacional), incluindo os consumidores. As baterias armazenam energia produzida quando há maior oferta e a devolvem à rede nos períodos de aumento do consumo. Na geração solar, podem ser carregadas durante o dia e acionadas no início da noite, quando a produção solar diminui e a demanda é maior. O armazenamento ajuda a reduzir o desperdício e dá flexibilidade ao sistema, permitindo equilibrar rapidamente geração e consumo. Ainda assim, não substitui os investimentos necessários para ampliar as redes de transmissão e distribuição.

artigo.texto: Hinojosa calls for data center moratorium as Perry files Senate bill Governor-Elect wants pause on new permits; state senator’s bill would set water, power and tax rules LUBBOCK, Texas (KCBD) - New Democrat Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa said she wants a statewide moratorium on new data centers, but she acknowledged she does not have the power to stop data centers already under construction. Hinojosa made the comments Thursday evening as a guest on the Fox News Channel, where she described her plan for the growing industry. Hinojosa: ‘A seat at the table’ Hinojosa said Texas lacks laws to protect residents and called for a ban on new data center permits until such laws pass. “We don’t have laws to protect Texans, and so my position is we need a moratorium, a ban on new data center permits until we pass laws to protect Texans, and most importantly, so that Texans can have a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into their communities.” Hinojosa said. “I have already heard from some people in the industry, they think that’s reasonable.” Perry files bill with 16 co-authors Lubbock state Sen. Charles Perry has filed a bill aimed at data center regulations. The bill lists 16 other co-authors, which shows a majority of support in the Senate. All but one of the co-authors are Republicans. Perry’s proposal would apply only to new data centers after Sept. 1 of next year. It would restrict them to four types of cooling focused on preserving fresh water. The bill would require every new data center to give state regulators an estimate of its water needs and its actual use each year. The bill would give the Public Utility Commission the power to set limits on water, light, noise and setbacks from other property. A facility that does not meet the requirements could not connect to the Texas power grid. The bill also would prevent any city, county or school district from giving a data center more than a 50% property tax break. Rodriquez: Legislature should set limits A group based in Abilene that opposes data centers called the bill “shallow.” Riley Rodriquez, who lost the Senate District 28 election to Perry earlier this month, said the Legislature should set the resource restrictions, not the Public Utility Commission. Rodriquez made the comments in a statement from the organization Don’t Drain Texas. Rodriquez also said the bill would still allow a facility to use a city’s water supply without limitations, as long as it reports the use to the state. Other proposals Lawmakers have filed dozens of other proposals in the House and Senate focused on data center regulation. Perry’s bill has the most support in the Senate. The Legislature will convene Jan. 12. Copyright 2026 KCBD. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Ford starts shipping CATL battery cells from Michigan plant Ford has shipped its first CATL battery cells from Michigan, a milestone dogged by political scrutiny of the Chinese tie-up and shaky quarterly profits. In this article 3 sections Ford Motor Co (NYSE: F) has shipped its first CATL battery cells from a Michigan factory, a concrete step in a strategy the carmaker has pursued since 2023 but one that remains politically fraught in Washington. The cells, manufactured using technology licensed from China’s CATL, left the BlueOval Battery Park in Marshall, Michigan, on Wednesday 18 November 2026, bound for the Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky, where they will power pre-production units of Ford’s new Fathom electric pickup, as UPI reported. The cells are lithium iron phosphate, or LFP – a battery chemistry that trades some energy density for lower cost and longer cycle life, and one that Chinese manufacturers have dominated for years. Ford’s VP of advanced development, Alan Clarke, said CATL’s scale made it “the best supplier” to help the company learn the chemistry quickly, framing the licensing arrangement as a fast-track rather than a dependency, according to UPI. A licence, not a joint venture – Ford insists The structural distinction matters because it has become the crux of a running argument in Washington. Ford has been explicit that the Marshall plant is wholly owned and operated by the carmaker, which employs the workforce and runs the supply chain, with CATL providing technology and services under contract rather than equity, according to reporting from CarPro. That framing has not satisfied every critic in the current administration. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the department “remains deeply alarmed by Ford’s continued reliance on licensed technology from Chinese battery manufacturer CATL” at the Marshall facility, according to InsideEVs. Ford’s response, as relayed by the same outlet, was that the arrangement is “a limited technology-licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation” – a rebuttal that effectively concedes the political sensitivity even as it rejects the characterisation. CATL’s presence on a Pentagon list of companies alleged to have military ties has kept that scrutiny alive since the deal was first struck, per CarPro. For Ford, Marshall is as much a test of whether a US-owned plant running licensed Chinese chemistry can pass political muster as it is a manufacturing milestone. The scale Ford is chasing Ford says the Michigan lines can run at 40 cells a minute, which the company describes as among the fastest LFP prismatic production rates outside China, according to Yahoo Finance. The Detroit News reported the plant is designed to eventually run two such lines at full ramp-up. The facility itself represents a $3 billion investment, according to the International Business Times, with production having quietly begun in October before Wednesday’s shipment made the milestone public. Ford’s own target is to begin assembling cells into finished battery packs at a neighbouring facility in 2027, with the first production Fathom pickups reaching buyers by the end of that year, according to Fox17/WOOD-TV, which also reported that Michigan governor Gretchen Whitmer attended the launch and credited state support for landing the project. Ford’s long-term goal for the site is roughly 1,700 jobs, more than 70% of them drawn from the Marshall, Albion and Battle Creek area, the same report said. A milestone against an uneven balance sheet The announcement lands at an awkward moment for Ford’s core profitability. The carmaker’s quarterly net income has swung sharply over the past two years – from a $1.92 billion profit in the second quarter of 2023 to a $36 million net loss in the second quarter of 2025, before returning to diluted earnings per share of $0.50 in the third quarter of 2026, according to Ford’s own filings with the SEC. Quarterly revenue has moved in a similarly uneven band, from $40.7 billion in the first quarter of 2025 to $50.5 billion a couple of quarters later, per the same disclosures. Battery self-sufficiency is, in that context, as much a cost-control bet as a technology one: LFP chemistry is cheaper than the nickel-based cells Ford has relied on, and bringing production onshore is meant to insulate the company from both tariff exposure and supply shocks further down the line. Markets, for their part, treated the news as background noise rather than a catalyst. Ford shares closed at $11.31, down 0.57% on the day and down 5.31% over the preceding 20 trading sessions, with volume running at 1.12 times the 20-day average – a pattern consistent with the stock’s existing short-term drift rather than a reaction unique to the battery news. What happens next is less about the shipment itself than about what comes after it. Ford has pointed to 2027 as the year it expects to move from shipping test cells to assembling full packs at Marshall, and ultimately to putting Fathom pickups built on this chemistry into customers’ hands. Whether the licensing structure it has built around CATL can survive sustained political pressure in Washington may end up mattering as much to that timeline as the engineering does. artigo.texto: LEEDS, England, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Matrix will retain majority stakes in both projects. The Fund's investment will support development and delivery. Over 200 construction and operation jobs are expected to be created or supported. Along key transmission corridors between Scotland and England, the projects will provide 1GW of capacity and 2GWh of energy storage. They will enhance grid flexibility, manage network constraints and enable integration of renewable energy, supporting the UK's clean energy objectives. Eccles construction is underway, with commercial operations expected in October 2027. Kilmarnock construction is expected to begin in December 2026, with operations targeted for September 2028. The investment builds on the Fund's energy storage track record and role in mobilising private capital for the UK's energy transition. The projects underpin Matrix' UK strategy, with plans for further investment in generation and storage. Oliver Holbourn, CEO of the National Wealth Fund, said: "Battery storage is critical to a cleaner, more secure and flexible energy system. Investing alongside Matrix Renewables, the Fund helps unlock two nationally significant projects that will store more renewable power, strengthen grid links between Scotland and England, and support hundreds of jobs." Luis Sabaté, CEO at Matrix, said: "These projects mark Matrix' first UK investments in one of the world's most advanced energy storage markets. Matrix plans further multi-gigawatt investments in storage and flexible generation, diversifying its portfolio. The partnership with the National Wealth Fund reflects project quality and shared commitment to advancing large-scale UK energy storage." Exchequer Secretary and Minister for Growth Dan Tomlinson said: "Scotland is at the heart of Britain's clean energy future. The Fund's investment will support hundreds of jobs in Eccles and Kilmarnock, strengthen Britain's energy security and help deliver needed infrastructure to drive growth in more places across the UK." artigo.texto: EU 2040 Climate Goal Faces Pressure From Carbon Market Compromise A leaked document reviewed by Euronews indicates that reforms to the European Union's Emissions Trading System could weaken the bloc's 2040 climate target. The Irish Presidency of the EU Council has softened a proposal set for discussion by EU ambassadors on Wednesday, as political pressure mounts over reconciling emissions goals with industrial competitiveness and high energy costs. The compromise text aims to secure political backing for the carbon market beyond 2030, but climate advocates caution that concessions meant to protect European industry may reduce the system's contribution to the 2040 target, leaving other economic sectors to cover the gap. Free Allowances and Investment Plans The Council text keeps the European Commission's July proposal to slow the decline in carbon allowances, extend free permits for industry and bring international carbon credits into the EU market so that domestic emissions can be offset through projects abroad. Under the Irish Presidency's proposal, industrial companies would retain 80 percent of their free allowances if they submit an investment plan, even if they later fail to carry out the proposed decarbonisation investments. The remaining 20 percent would depend on starting construction of eligible projects. Free allowances are permits companies receive without buying them at auction, designed to shield EU producers from competition in countries with less stringent climate rules, such as China and the United States. The proposal represents a significant political concession to industries worried about losing those allowances and raises questions about whether the ETS will provide enough incentive to cut emissions. International Credits and the 2040 Target On international carbon credits, the Council has retained the Commission's proposal to set aside allowances equivalent to 260 million tonnes of CO2 to finance their purchase. It also leaves open a possible pilot phase between 2031 and 2035 to test the system before full implementation. The Council has maintained stringent quality and integrity requirements for international credits, making the ETS reduction trajectory increasingly dependent on their availability. If industries cannot buy them, the 2040 climate target could be jeopardised, since it requires at least an 85 percent domestic net emissions reduction, with international credits accounting for the remaining 5 percent. Negotiation Timeline and Member State Divisions The Irish Presidency is seeking consensus among the 27 EU countries before talks move to more politically sensitive questions of climate ambition and burden-sharing. It hopes to secure an agreement at the Environment Council on December 11, while the European Parliament is expected to vote during its December 14-17 plenary session in Strasbourg. The presidency faces an uphill battle given deep divisions among member states and the complexity of the negotiations. According to a second document reviewed by Euronews, EU countries are already divided over how quickly carbon permit supply should shrink, whether companies should use international credits to meet obligations and how far industrial sectors should be shielded from rising carbon costs. Taken together, these demands risk diluting the ETS when it is expected to drive a large share of the bloc's next phase of emissions cuts. Governments generally want to preserve the ETS as a source of revenue for decarbonisation, but concerns are growing about costs imposed on energy-intensive industries competing with manufacturers in China or the United States. Some capitals argue permit numbers should decline to raise carbon pricing and encourage divestment from fossil fuels, while others fear the impact of withdrawing free allowances on struggling industries. A slower reduction would ease pressure on power plants and factories, potentially tempering carbon prices and giving companies more time to adapt, but it would also mean fewer emissions cuts in ETS-covered sectors, making the 2040 target harder to reach. Analysis Questions Reform Compatibility A recent analysis by the Oko-Institut, commissioned by the environmental campaign group WWF Germany, warned that the Commission's proposed ETS reform is incompatible with the EU target of cutting net emissions by 90 percent by 2040. Lisa Okken, an industrial policy expert at WWF Germany, said the Commission was choosing to take risks on climate protection rather than safeguard the future of European industry, and argued that the proposed reform lacks the carbon price signal needed to drive urgent modernisation. She said the gap was being filled with complicated accounting measures and excessive flexibility. Environmentalists also cited concern over a proposal to allow additional emissions beyond the existing cap in exchange for future permanent carbon removals through expensive technologies designed to capture CO2 from the air. The study noted that it remains unclear whether such removals can be delivered at the required scale, since the necessary capacity does not exist today. - 1. artigo.texto: Dive Brief: - State ratepayer advocates have joined the PJM Interconnection’s market monitor in calling for the grid operator to delay its upcoming capacity auction over concerns it could threaten the reliability of the bulk power system and cause consumers to pay billions in unnecessary costs driven by data centers. - Representatives from seven states, including Pennsylvania, Ohio and New Jersey, urged PJM’s board in a letter Wednesday to postpone the base capacity auction for the 2029/30 delivery year — set to be held Dec. 9 to Dec. 15 — “until data center loads, both real and speculative, can be removed from the load forecast” and the grid operator holds a separate reliability backstop procurement for the large loads. - The letter cited a Nov. 12 report from the independent market monitor, Monitoring Analytics, that warned PJM’s forecast includes data centers that have been canceled or are unlikely to reach projected demand levels, which could impose an additional $5 billion to $10 billion on PJM’s 67 million consumers. The grid operator would need to seek approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to delay the auction. Dive Insight: The request from the ratepayer advocates comes amid nationwide concern about energy affordability and data centers, as reflected in the midterm elections. The letter says that given “the urgency of the approaching auction,” its signatories request a written response from PJM’s board no later than Nov. 23. In PJM, affordability concerns have been driven by a recent spike in capacity prices caused by growing data center load forecasts. PJM’s current capacity market rules effectively prevent data center companies from paying for their own power supply and infrastructure costs. PJM recognizes the financial impacts rising electricity bills place on households and businesses, Jeffrey Shields, a spokesman for the grid operator, told Utility Dive in an email. “The December auction includes an established price cap, providing an important safeguard against how high prices can rise,” he said. “The system urgently needs capacity to meet rising demand. Postponing the auction this close to its execution could destabilize the market and increase the risk of power interruptions when customers need electricity most.” Electricity demand is growing faster than new power supplies can be built, according to Shields. “While decisions about whether data centers and other large electricity users can connect to the grid rest with policymakers and utilities, PJM must plan for the demand those decisions create.” Shields said. “That means moving forward with securing the power we need while continuing to advance solutions that address the challenges of growing demand and the pressure on electricity costs.” So far, including existing and forecast data center demand in PJM’s capacity market has increased capacity costs by $29.4 billion for all customers, according to Monitoring Analytics’ Nov. 12 report that called for the auction to be postponed. PJM has responded to pressure from states, federal regulators and consumers by proposing a two-part plan to meet data center demand by facilitating bilateral contracts outside its normal capacity auctions, and also holding a backstop procurement for large loads that do not have bilateral contracts. It is also pursuing reforms to its rules for interconnecting large loads and generating supplies. The status of these efforts is pending. The market monitor’s concerns were amplified by Exelon’s Nov. 3 complaint at FERC that challenged PJM’s three-year forward auction, partly over the uncertainty in forecasting data center load and the resulting billions in potential excess capacity costs, the ratepayer advocates said. The advocates noted that PJM plans to publish the final “planning parameters” for the upcoming auction, which may remove canceled or delayed data center projects from the auction’s demand curve, on Nov. 19. However, the market monitor’s recommendation is not simply to update PJM’s load forecast, they added. “It is to fundamentally change how forecasted data-center demand is treated in the capacity auction so that existing consumers are not required to subsidize speculative or uncommitted data center demand,” the advocates said. “The delay would allow PJM to implement the IMM recommendations, subject to FERC approval and appropriate reliability safeguards.” A “statement of principles” endorsed in January by PJM and the governors of its 13 states emphasized that large-load forecasts must be “real and verified,” the ratepayer advocates said. “Proceeding with an auction that incorporates both real and speculative data-center demand, despite the [market monitor’s] findings, would undermine that commitment and expose consumers to billions in potentially avoidable costs.” The letter was sent to PJM by the Office of the Ohio Consumers’ Counsel, the Delaware Public Advocate, the West Virginia Consumer Advocate, the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel, the Pennsylvania Office of Consumer Advocate, the New Jersey Division of Rate Counsel, the Illinois Attorney General’s Office and the Illinois Citizens Utility Board.

artigo.texto: Orangeburg forum explores artificial intelligence, data centers ORANGEBURG, S.C. (WIS) - State Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter hosted a public education forum on artificial intelligence and data centers at Orangeburg-Calhoun Technical College. The aim of the forum was to bring community members together to learn about the technology before making quick judgements. “I suspect, like me, there are a lot of people who are using it that don’t really recognize it. The point tonight is to simply connect the dots, educate the community and be able to make informed decisions,” said Cobb-Hunter. The forum followed Orangeburg County’s September approval of a moratorium halting new data center development and applications for at least 12 months. Elected officials, technology professionals and infrastructure representatives participated in the discussion. Warren Harley, general manager of the city of Orangeburg’s Department of Public Utilities, said no plans are in motion for a data center at this time. He said any data center seeking to use the utility’s system would pay the cost of service rather than passing it on to customers. “Whatever we do with respect to data centers or any big customer, that it doesn’t negatively impact our system or the customers we serve, from a rate perspective, from a cost perspective,” Harley said. “Any data center looking to come on to our system, whatever cost it is to serve, they will pay the cost and we will not pass that on to the customer.” Orangeburg resident Rick Leonard said the discussion changed his thinking about the technology and its potential impact. “I’m glad we’re taking a positive step, not just saying no and instead saying, ‘This might be a great thing and I don’t want us to miss the boat,’” Leonard said. Cobb-Hunter said she is working to host a similar event in the near future. Feel more informed, prepared, and connected with WIS.
